chapters.title: Chapter 5589: Nature Against Nature!
paragraphs: The white weapons fell!

Lances of woven loomlight rained down from the many-sided head of the Woe Culture as turning wheels of stellar white carved through the unseen sky, and the nine clones of THE True Human Emperor scattered across the heavens as detonations of crimson gold met an authority older than the frameworks themsleves!
And through all of it, the vast thing was still trying to understand.
"You strike me even now,"its heavy voice boomed as three of its long legs swept a clone out of the sky, hair-fine threads bending fortune so that every dodge arrived a breath late!

"And I strike you, because you would end me, and I preserve myself. But I do not understand you, Little One! This... is what I am? I am a Woe Culture? I am simply living as I should, emulating the Primevals and THE First Lifeforms. You would hunt me because of my nature? Others have passed through here and seen me and not done anything. We simply nod to each other. Why not you?"
Others!
The word boomed inside Noah even as his clones wove between falling lances. Others had passed through this unseen layer.
Others had seen this thing hanging over his people, and nodded, and moved along! What manner of beings strolled through the white rivers above the skies of Dimensions unobserved?
"I do not hunt you because having a nature is a crime. Everything alive has one. I hunt you because your nature and mine conflict, and conflicting natures do not get to share one sky!"
"Natures do not conflict," the Woe Culture cut in, a lance of white driving down between two clones as it spoke, genuinely arguing now, fighting and reasoning in the same breath!
"Natures coexist. The storm does not conflict with the mountain."
"The storm does not FARM the mountain!"Noah’s nine voices cracked back across the sky as staffs swept a wheel of white aside!

"Your nature farms the grief of gathered lifeforms. My nature is to gather lifeforms and guard them. The ones you drink from below are mine, sworn to me, led by me, and every ribbon of misery you pull up through those jaws is pulled out of my people! Those others who nodded at you carried no one beneath your shadow. I do. Your claim on this sky and my claim on this sky cannot both stand."
His voice went cold as a drop of blood formed at every staff. "So one of them falls. You will not die for being what you are. You die for being what you are...HERE."
HUUM!
The violet lights churned slowly through the endless body as its legs drew back, and when it spoke again, there was something almost reasonable in the vast voice.
"Then I will leave here. I will go elsewhere, and live my nature above some other sky."
"You will do the same where you go, yes?"
"Of course,"the Woe Culture said honestly, without a single beat of hesitation, "for that is my nature."
And there it was.

It would drift across the unseen layer and settle above some other Dimension of countless decillions who buried their dead and never knew why the wars kept coming, and it would open its jaws, and it saw nothing in that sentence to apologize for.
Noah shook his head as before any sentence could be carried out, he reached for his newest tool.
THE Yoke of the Standing Sky!

The invisible structure across his shoulders woke for the first time as he willed it, blue gold force spreading out from him through all nine clones at once, and nine titanic figures raised their hands toward the endless purple body as Noah did something no being below had ever done to a Woe Culture.
He took it up.
BOOM!
The weight arrived!

Gigaparsecs of living lifeform came down onto his existence in a single instant as the Yoke gathered the whole of it, plates and legs and gigaparsecs of glowing skin, every league of a thing vaster than an Observable Existence, and Noah felt his frame ring from his clones to his true body on a distant volcanic peak! His shoulders bent!

The three singularities in his depths flared as his PONDUS was pressed to its edges for the first time since crossing, and the question of what the Yoke could bear was being answered in the harshest classroom there was!
Could he hold a lifeform the size of an endless sky?
His spine, seated with the Telos of Paradox, held opposing weights without breaking. His shoulders, broad with the Yoke, held the rest!

And the Woe Culture thrashed in shock as its entire body lifted, because it was being CARRIED, hoisted off the domain it had grazed for ages by something a fraction of a fraction of its size, its legs kicking at nothing, its fortune-threads finding no odds to bend against a grip that was not an attack at all!
"What... what is this?! Put me down, Little One! PUT ME DOWN!"
"As you wish,"Noah said.
And he threw it.
BOOM!
Nine clones pivoted as one as the carried weight swung, and THE True Human Emperor hurled a lifeform countless gigaparsecs wide out of the unseen sky of THE Ymnaros entirely!

The endless purple body tore upward through the layer, through the white rivers, through the skin of the Dimension itself, and was flung countless gigaparsecs out into the dark, tumbling end over end over end, until it crashed to a stop far beyond any sky, in the foamy space between Dimensions!

Black foam churned around its sprawled bulk in slow enormous bubbles, the void between all things frothing where a Dimension’s weight had landed in it, and before the Woe Culture could even right itself, nine folds of crimson gold opened in the dark around it.
The clones had followed.

Nine crowns of blood turned in the foamy black as nine staffs rose, and blood began to gather at every one. Not in drops now. In seas! Millions of Sanguine Blood Drops condensed around each titanic figure as the space between Dimensions filled with crimson gold rain waiting to fall, and below them the Woe Culture gathered its legs beneath it and reached desperately for the white rivers that threaded even here, even through the foam, because the Argent Loom flowed through the spaces between as surely as it flowed through everything!
"I too shall have to live truly to my nature,"Noah said quietly, "as my heart and mind tell me... You must die."
BOOM!
The rain fell!

Millions of Blood Drops from each clone tore down through the churning foam as the body of the Woe Culture vanished beneath detonations without number, event horizons blooming across gigaparsecs of stellar purple as plates shattered and clear skin ruptured and violet lights burst in waves!
And it endured!

The Argent Loom poured into it from every direction as white rivers bent out of their courses and flooded its wounds. Loomlight knitted faster than crimson could tear! Lattices of white rose around its many-sided head and DRANK the detonations whole!
And for the first time since his transformation, Noah felt his own power struggle.

His blood detonated against woven loomlight, and the loomlight refused to be commanded, refused to be corrupted, refused even to properly break. He had felled a vessel of THE Sealed One with two drops. He had cleared armies with one. And this relatively harmless thing, this grazer, wrapped in the Loom, was costing him millions! The comparison told him everything about what flowed through those white rivers.
So Noah stopped holding back the only thing he had that it did not.
He filled his Provenance Essence into his blood completely!

All three singularities poured themselves through the connection to his clones as every remaining drop in the foamy dark ignited from within, stellar blue blazing up through crimson gold, blood that was no longer merely his resource but his very light given liquid form!
And when the next wave of drops fell, they did not detonate against the loomlight walls.
They passed through them.

Because the Loom was an authority, and grand beyond measure, but it was still a thing that flowed OUTSIDE of lifeforms, a river to be used! And his blood now carried the one thing in all of existence that answered to nothing outside itself. He had Provenance. This creature did not. That was the entire difference, and today, it was the entire battle!

The white lattices parted around his burning drops as loomlight slid off stellar blue without purchase, and the detonations landed on flesh that could no longer knit itself closed, and gorges became canyons became severings as the endless body of the Woe Culture came apart across the foam!
And it cried out.

The sound rolled through the space between Dimensions, mournful and vast and utterly without anger, the grief-drinker grieving at last on its own behalf as its violet lights guttered out along thousands of Gigaparsecs.
"How could you end me... for simply living by my nature? I curse you... I curse you...!"
Its body burst.

Countless light years of stellar purple, gigaparsecs of plates and legs and clear glowing skin, ruptured outward in slow silence and dissolved, breaking down into indicernable motes of violet that scattered across the black foam and thinned and went dark.

The nine clones of THE True Human Emperor floated amid the dissolution and gazed upon it, crowns of blood turning, saying nothing, as the largest lifeform Noah had ever killed stopped existing in the space between Dimensions, far from any sky it could ever graze again.
And Noah, through nine sets of senses at once, probed the dying words.

I curse you. Had that been a wail, or a working? He swept his sight across his clones, across his blood, across the connection running back to his body on a volcanic peak, hunting for any thread of violet that had latched where it should not have. He found nothing.
Which meant nothing had landed, or that whatever had landed was not a thing his senses knew how to find yet.
HUUM!

|The Woe Culture has been granted its death. Its nature has ended with it: the probability-tendrils woven across THE Golden Expanse and its surrounding regions have unraveled. The adversity it farmed will no longer be called. Your Provenance Essence has increased in concentration. Your PONDUS has increased. PONDUS: 12.|
|A separate matter, Master.|

|Due to settings enacted by THE Infiniverse, THE Tide That Owes Nothing has been quietly generating and preserving potential boons for all things you have given, for a while now. Leadership given to a domain. Protection given to millions. Marks given to the marked. Affirmation given to the grieving. The ledger has been kept, and none of it has yet been answered.|
|With the granting of death to a unique lifeform, the Tide has reached an unprecedented generation.|
|Shall the generation and preservation continue?|

The nine clones of THE True Human Emperor floated amid the dissolution and gazed upon it, crowns of blood turning, saying nothing, as the largest lifeform Noah had ever killed stopped existing in the space between Dimensions, far from any sky it could ever graze again.
And Noah, through nine sets of senses at once, probed the dying words.
I curse you.
Had that been a wail, or a working?
He swept his sight across his clones, across his blood, across the connection running back to his body on a volcanic peak, hunting for any thread of violet that had latched where it should not have.
He found nothing.
Which meant nothing had landed, or that whatever had landed was not a thing his senses knew how to find yet.
HUUM!

The adversity it farmed will no longer be called.
Your Provenance Essence has increased in concentration.
Your PONDUS has increased.
PONDUS: 12.|

|Due to settings enacted by THE Infiniverse, THE Tide That Owes Nothing has been quietly generating and preserving potential boons for all things you have given, for a while now.
Leadership given to a domain.
Protection given to millions.
Marks given to the marked.
Affirmation given to the grieving.
The ledger has been kept, and none of it has yet been answered.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5590: Wrong Place, Wrong Time!
paragraphs: <THE Sealed One>
Deep within THE Infinite Carcosa, a temple rose out of a sea of golden mist.

It was built of white stone in tiers upon tiers, each tier wide enough to hold a city, and across its endless steps and colonnades, True Lifeforms moved about in the plain robes of priests! Hundreds of them!

Beings whose presense would have flattened Observable Existences walked in silent lines carrying censers and sealed urns, tending rows of caged radiances that pulsed behind lattice screens, and every one of them moved with bowed heads, because the master of this temple had been old before their Ages had names.
At the very top of the temple, on a wide platform open to the golden mist, a humanoid Primeval One sat on a plain stone seat.

He wore the shape of a broad old man with skin the color of river clay, hairless, heavy-shouldered, dressed in a single white cloth, and his eyes held the slow patience of something that had watched harvests of entire Ages come and go.

This was one of the old harvesters. One of those who had stood behind the Gilded Lifeforms across the Ages as they reaped First Causes from the young and the dying, gathering the yield into temples exactly of this kind.
And onto the platform before him, without sound or ceremony, a figure appeared.
A tall pale man in layered dark robes, lean and unhurried, looking around calmly at the tiers and the priests and the caged lights with the mild interest of a buyer in a familiar market.
THE Sealed One had arrived.
The Primeval One smiled slowly.
"Now what," he said, "would bring a vile thing like you to my steps?"

"Is that any way to greet an old customer?"The vessel of THE Sealed One clasped its hands behind its back."I bought from this temple when it had four tiers. I remember when your priests were seven frightened Gilded children."
"And I remember what you paid with." The old man’s smile did not move. "Which is why I ask what brings you, instead of asking you to leave. Speak your business."
The Sealed One drifted a step along the platform, gaze trailing across the caged radiances below.
"I came to make things easy on myself."The pale man turned, and his voice settled into the tone of a man laying goods on a table.

"I have too many avenues where I must place my focus. Too many boards, too many pieces, and recently, a new expense I did not plan for. So I have come to hand you an opportunity, and let your nature do my work. Consider it a gift between old friends."
"You have never given a gift in your existence."
"And you have never refused one. Listen."The vessel raised one finger.

"A Remnant Existential Treasure has surfaced. Not a rumor. Not a fragment. A true Remnant, whole, worn openly. It sits in THE Ymnaros Dimension, in the hands of a lifeform that is just now growing into its power. Young. Unguarded. Unclaimed by any faction you would have to answer to." He smiled thinly.

"I wanted to use you as a sharp sword, harvester, because my hands are full, and because I want this enemy of mine to suffer. Noah Osmont, in THE Ymnaros Dimension... holds a Remnant Existential Treasure."
The words settled over the platform, and below, several priests paused mid-step.
A Remnant Existential Treasure! The kind of prize that emptied temples and started wars between Primeval Ones, offered up freely with a name and an address attached!
The old man looked at the pale vessel for a long moment.
And then the Primeval One smiled wider than he had smiled all Age.
"It is a good plot that you had," he said warmly. "It truly is. It is just a shame... that you came here at the wrong, wrong time."
The moment the words finished, the air above the platform moved.
Unseen white authority descended!

THE Argent Loom, rivers of it, bent down out of the golden mist where no eye had marked them and wrapped around the body of THE Sealed One’s vessel in silent coils, and before the pale man could so much as flinch, someone appeared behind him.
A hand reached past his shoulder.
And a collar closed around his neck!
CLICK!

The change was instsntly and total. The waves of Intent that forever rolled off the vessel of THE Sealed One faded away! His Infinity, silent and compounding beneath every body he had ever worn, went dark! The deep patient weight of the Primordial Source drained out of his frame like water out of an unstoppered basin, and what remained standing on the platform, in layered dark robes, was a body that read to every sense in existence as a normal human with absolutely no authority at all.
The vessel’s hands rose slowly to his own neck.

The collar was a seamless band of pale gray metal, cool and light, without lock or hinge or joint, and across its surface, thread-fine lines of white ran in woven patterns, loomlight hardened into a shape. It did not burn him. It did not bind his limbs. It simply sat there, quiet as a closed door, and on its far side sat everything he had ever been.
He looked down at it with a heavy, heavy gaze.
"Hm. I did not expect to bag one of the vessels of THE Sealed One here."
The voice came from behind him, and he turned.

A woman stood on the platform. She was tall, dressed in simple pale garments without ornament, dark hair bound back plainly, and she was terrifying for one reason above all others: she emanated nothing.

Not a glimmer of authority. Not a thread of Intent, not a breath of any Source, not one single register on any instrument his stripped senses had ever owned. There was only THE Argent Loom, flowing around her in slow white rivers, orbiting her frame the way rivers orbit nothing else in existence, and her pale eyes studied him with unhurried interest.

"This particular body of yours should have low dimensionality," she said, walking a slow circle around him. "It shouldn’t have sensed anything. And it should be cut off entirely from your main ones. No records out. No memories back. You build your vessels carefully, I will grant you that."
She stopped in front of him, and tilted her head. "But we can still torture you, to obtain information. Hmm."
She turned from him, crossed the platform, and did something that struck the stripped vessel harder than the collar had.
She walked to the Primeval One, and stroked the top of his ancient head.

The old harvester, a being who had stood behind the reaping of Ages, sat perfectly still under her hand, eyes lowered, and around his own thick neck, half-hidden by the white cloth, a band of pale gray metal caught the light!
"The age of lifeforms utilizing and abusing authority is coming to an end," the woman said, her hand resting on the Primeval One’s head as she looked out over the temple tiers.

"Intents. Sources. Infinities. Causes. For long enough, existence has bent and bled beneath beings who were handed power by frameworks and used it as they pleased. That ends now. You have simply joined the many of you that we will round up, and shackle, and make incapable of utilizing any ounce of authority... to finally bring stability across existence."She smiled, small and cold.
"Rejoice, oh Sealed One. For you will join many others."
And as she said it, the golden mist around the temple flashed with white!
Rivers of THE Argent Loom lit up across the whole horizon as veils that had hung there unseen came down, and metallic structures were revealed on every side!
Cubical prisons of dull gray metal, stacked upon each other in columns and walls and mountains of cells, rising out of the mist tier upon tier upon tier!
The vessel of THE Sealed One squinted through eyes that were merely human now.
And inside the cells, he saw them.

Thousands upon thousands of lifeforms! Infinite Lifeforms and Gilded Lifeforms with their silent seas gone dark! Source Lifeforms, dense and patient no longer! Even ancient True Lifeforms, beings whose names held weight across THE Infinite Carcosa, sitting in chained collars in bare metal cells, and not one of them emanated any authority at all, and their eyes, every pair of eyes down every corridor of stacked cells, showed the same three things.
Despair. Horror. Fear!
"A new age is coming... a new age is coming, as many wrongs will be corrected."

The voice of that terrifying woman echoed out across the golden mist, calm and certain, and the vessel of THE Sealed One stood collared at the top of the temple and looked out at the true scale of the place he had walked into, because the stacked cubical prisons did not end at the horizon.
They continued past it, wall after mountain after wall of caged authority, stretching out around this entire place for gigaparsecs in every direction!
The golden mist rolled against the temple tiers, and against the walls of stacked cells beyond them, and at the top of it all, the two captors spoke over their prize.
"You heard his offering, Ohmran." The woman stood at the platform’s edge with the white rivers turning slowly around her.
"A Remnant Existential Treasure. Worn openly, in THE Ymnaros, by a lifeform still growing into its power."

"I heard it, Warden Yrsa."The old clay-skinned Primeval One rose from his stone seat, and standing, he was half again the height of a titan, thick and slow and heavy-footed, the pale gray band glinting at his throat beneath the white cloth.
Yrsa turned from the mist, and the vessel of THE Sealed One, collared and stripped and merely human, watched her plain face as she thought.
"A Remnant cannot be left in random hands. So..."She looked up at the towering old one.

"Check this out, Ohmran. Go to THE Ymnaros. Verify the treasure and the holder. Observe. Touch nothing that is not confirmed, and engage nothing that is. You carry my leash and my patience, and only one of them is long."
The Primeval One bowed his heavy head.
"As the Warden says."

He stepped off the platform, and the golden mist swallowed a being who had stood behind the reaping of Ages, sent now as an errand-runner with a collar under his cloth, and the vessel of THE Sealed One watched it happen.
Then Yrsa turned to him.
"Now," she said. "You."
She crossed the platform without hurry, and took his right hand in both of hers, almost gently, the way one takes the hand of an elder at a bedside.
And she broke it.
CRACK!

The sound rolled across the platform as bones that were merely human bones gave way in her grip, and the vessel of THE Sealed One made a noise he had not made in Ages, because there was no Intent to seal the pain away, no Infinity to compound beneath it, no Source to drink it down! There was only a hand, and a broken hand hurt!
"Interesting," Yrsa said, watching his face with mild attention. "You feel it fully. Your main bodies truly receive nothing from this one. That is fine workmanship."
She let the ruined hand drop, and took the left.
"Let us speak of THE Dimensionlapses."
CRACK!
"The collapsing of Dimensions into one another. The fusings. The falls. Whole skies folding into other skies while their lifeforms drown between."Her voice never rose, never quickened.
"It has accelerated this Age, and the pattern is not natural..."
CRACK!

"So." She looked up at him from below, pale eyes patient, hands already moving to the last unbroken limb. "What do you know regarding THE Dimensionlapses? Is it just you behind them... or are there others?"
The Sealed One had a heavy gaze as he did everything he could not to scream in pain, and he forced himself to utter out...
"Do you know who you are making an enemy of? I am-"
CRACK!
Another limb was broken as the woman before him looked down coldly.

"I don’t give a damn who you are, O Riven. O Sealed One. I will throw you in a prison to bleed out and die soon enough as before that, you will answer my questions. Oh, you are fully...a lifeform with no power by the way, so my end move is a simple one of extracting your memories. But sadly...many records are kept with a mixture of authorities as I will fry your brain and kill you when I do and gain a few tidbits. So before that, I like for you to talk freely. So...talk."
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5591: What Reigns Supreme?
paragraphs: <THE Sealed One>
Talk.

The word hung in the golden mist as the vessel of THE Sealed One stood on four broken foundations, blood running freely down his wrists and pooling in his shoes, and instead of answering her, he lifted his merely human eyes and gazed up at the prisons.

They went on and on. Wall after mountain after wall of stacked gray cells, and in every cell, a face! An Infinite Lifeform staring at nothing as its silent seas stayed dark. A Gilded one with its brilliance snuffed, hugging its own knees. Source Lifeforms pressed against metal, ancient True Lifeforms sitting perfectly still in the way of beings who had run out of things to try, and down every corridor, in every direction, for gigaparsecs, those same three tenants living in every pair of eyes.
Despair. Horror. Fear!
"I will talk," the vessel said, and even bleeding, his voice found its old evenness. "Let us talk about you. Are you among the hypocrites, Warden? The ones who think they are doing something good?"
Yrsa said nothing, and he took the silence as a stage.

"There are a number of beings like me who move above the many. We sit behind thrones and beneath foundations, and we use authority and power to do our own bidding across Ages. I am guilty of everything you suspect and a great deal you lack the imagination for. If you shackled me, and told me you were banning the usage of authority for things like me who abuse it... that, I would understand. I would even call it overdue."

His broken hand rose an inch, gesturing at the horizon of cells. "But look at all of these innocent ones. Look at them! What did the millions, the billions of Infinite Lifeforms and Gilded ones and Source Lifeforms DO with their authority to deserve being chained like this? They grew as their natures grew them. They climbed the only ladders existence offered. And your answer to my crimes... is their cages."
And Warden Yrsa laughed at this time!
It was a real laugh, short and genuinely amused as she knew THE Sealed One didn’t give a damn about innocents and just wanted to waste time!

"Who are you," she said, "to even discuss morality? To sort which ones are innocent and which ones are not? The single greatest argument for my work is standing in front of me." She walked a slow half-circle around him.
"But fine. Let us grant your point fully. Let us say the vast majority of them are innocent. Truly innocent. Do you know what they are then?"
She stopped, and looked up at the cells.

"They are you, earlier. You rose from beings just like them. You were once a tiny little lifeform, climbing the only ladders existence offered, growing as your nature grew you. And yet look at what you grew up to be. Every horror above starts as an innocent below, and existence has run that experiment for eons and drowned in the results every single time. So no, I do not chain them for what they did. I chain them for what the ladder makes."

Her voice settled into something vast and level. "At this moment in time, we have begun the process. Binding, chaining, and removing authority across many Observable Existences and Dimensions, across THE Source Lands, across THE Infinite Carcosa. And when the bindings are done, every single one of them will be transferred to live peacefully across different regions of existence, in places where the abuse of authority cannot harm any other life."

"They can build their civilizations with their own hands. They can farm, and craft, and argue, and grow old. And if any of them ever wishes harm, they can, at most, harm themselves or a specific few. Never again will a single existence hold such an abuse of authority that it can affect the lives of countless others."
The vessel of THE Sealed One looked at her through the pain, bleeding from four broken limbs, and smiled.
"And look at you," he said softly."A single existence, deciding the fate of countless all around you, right now."
For one moment, the white rivers around her slowed.
Then Yrsa waved her hand, unbothered.
"I do not care for philosophy. I care for informstion. So we return to my questions, and you will notice that I have been patient."She crouched before him again.
"THE Dimensionlapses. The fusings accelerate this Age, and Dimensions do not fold into each other on their own schedule. Who benefits from skies drowning in skies? What is being consolidated? Speak."

"Mm. And here is my question."Blood was running from the corner of his mouth now, but the old pleasantness never left his voice. "What does a thing like you belong to? You wear no authority. You hate authority and yet use it. You collar Primevals and quote a coming age. So whose dog are you, Warden? A dog of Those Who Remain, sent to clean the board for its owners? Or something rarer... a dog of those who look down upon authority itself?"
His breath rattled, and his smile widened through it."Or are you a dog of THE First Lifeforms?"

"The conflicts between True Lifeforms and the Primeval Ones." Yrsa continued as if he had not spoken at all. "Three Ages of cold war warming. Someone has been feeding both sides of that fire. Was it you? Name your partners."
"You did not answer my question."
"Name the other hands behind THE Dimensionlapses."
"You did not answer my question." A wet laugh. "Which means the answer of who you belong to is...interesting. Merely a dog. Oh, a bitch, merely a bitch...that is all you are."
CRACK!

She broke a rib almost absently, and he folded around it, and still nothing came out of him but blood! Question after question, minutes of them, the fusings, the wars, his vessels, his allies, and the vessel of THE Sealed One deflected and asked and smiled and bled, growing paler by the exchange, his voice thinning as the pool beneath him spread, an ancient monster spending the last of a borrowed body on the only currency he had left.
Silence.
At last, Yrsa rose, and shook her head.
"I did not want to do it this way. Extraction through a fried brain wastes almost everything."She looked down at him.
"So. Memory extraction is the way to go. Any last words, as this vessel of yours is about to lose its life?"
The dying vessel lifted his head.
And he smiled with red teeth.
"Death... smiles at everyone," said THE Sealed One."I smile back at it."
BOOM!
Yrsa waved her hands.

Brilliant white authority flowed down out of the rivers and into the head of the vessel as his entire body began to seize, limbs hammering the platform, blood misting from his nose and ears, and through the seizure, through the frying of everything he was, his voice came out one last time, wet and shaking and utterly unafraid!

"Wait for me. Just wait for me... and I will show you how vast this existence is. I have been living across dimensions and time. My vessels are many. My connections are abundant. Just you... wait for me."
BOOM!
His body bled out of every orifice at once, and in the next moment, his head burst!

Yrsa frowned unpleasantly at the mess.

She waved her hand, and the ruined vessel of THE Sealed One turned to a drift of pale ash that the golden mist carried off the platform. What remained was the collar, and she caught it out of the air and held it, looking at the woven white lines in silence, reading what the extraction had pulled through them.
Then she shook her head with slow frustration.
"Barely any salvageable memories come out of this... haa!"
While she was expressing it, the rivers of THE Argent Loom around the platform slowed.

A handsome young man appeared out of the white, tall and clean-featured, and around his body circled halos of white light, ring after slow ring, orbiting him from shoulders to heels. His gaze was heavy as it settled on her.

"THE Sealed One is one of the major threats we keep tabs on across dimensions and time," he said. "Are we certain this one was entirely inhibited? That it did not get the chance to send any information back to its main components?"
Yrsa smiled slightly at that.

"Even he does not know that another vessel of his, alongside multiple vile but great minds of existence, inadvertently lent their help in making the design of these Existential Inhibitors possible. No, Axon. Nothing got through."She turned the collar once in her hand, and set it down on the empty stone seat.

"I will finish things up in this region of THE Infinite Carcosa. Can you actually go to THE Ymnaros Dimension, where Ohmran is already heading? Since THE Sealed One was there, and he faced a problem he wanted another to take care of... let us make sure it is not anything too major. And do not make a move unless you are absolutely certain of who is involved. We have begun locking up True Lifeforms, and even Primeval Lifeforms... but we have yet to start our hands on Descendants. We wait for further instructions before we make any moves on our own..."
"Understood."
The halos brightened, and Axon was gone into the white.

Yrsa stood alone at the top of the temple, and sighed, and looked out across the region. The tiers below her. The priests of a collared master. The mountains of cells running past every horizon, gigaparsecs of caged authority sitting in gray silence, millions of the mighty of existence waiting in small rooms for a peaceful age they had not asked for.
And she whispered to none of them.

"Existence breathes, and epochs pass, leaving Civilizations that become monuments, then crumble to memory, and are long forgotten when that breath comes again. In all these eons... just what reigns supreme?"

sentences.text: <THE Sealed One>
Talk.

The word hung in the golden mist as the vessel of THE Sealed One stood on four broken foundations, blood running freely down his wrists and pooling in his shoes, and instead of answering her, he lifted his merely human eyes and gazed up at the prisons.
They went on and on.
Wall after mountain after wall of stacked gray cells, and in every cell, a face!
An Infinite Lifeform staring at nothing as its silent seas stayed dark.
A Gilded one with its brilliance snuffed, hugging its own knees.

Source Lifeforms pressed against metal, ancient True Lifeforms sitting perfectly still in the way of beings who had run out of things to try, and down every corridor, in every direction, for gigaparsecs, those same three tenants living in every pair of eyes.
Despair.
Horror.
Fear!
"I will talk," the vessel said, and even bleeding, his voice found its old evenness.
"Let us talk about you.
Are you among the hypocrites, Warden?
The ones who think they are doing something good?"
Yrsa said nothing, and he took the silence as a stage.
"There are a number of beings like me who move above the many.
We sit behind thrones and beneath foundations, and we use authority and power to do our own bidding across Ages.
I am guilty of everything you suspect and a great deal you lack the imagination for.
If you shackled me, and told me you were banning the usage of authority for things like me who abuse it... that, I would understand.
I would even call it overdue."
His broken hand rose an inch, gesturing at the horizon of cells.
"But look at all of these innocent ones.
Look at them!
What did the millions, the billions of Infinite Lifeforms and Gilded ones and Source Lifeforms DO with their authority to deserve being chained like this?
They grew as their natures grew them.
They climbed the only ladders existence offered.
And your answer to my crimes... is their cages."
And Warden Yrsa laughed at this time!
It was a real laugh, short and genuinely amused as she knew THE Sealed One didn’t give a damn about innocents and just wanted to waste time!
"Who are you," she said, "to even discuss morality?
To sort which ones are innocent and which ones are not?
The single greatest argument for my work is standing in front of me." She walked a slow half-circle around him.
"But fine.
Let us grant your point fully.
Let us say the vast majority of them are innocent.
Truly innocent.
Do you know what they are then?"
She stopped, and looked up at the cells.
"They are you, earlier.
You rose from beings just like them.
You were once a tiny little lifeform, climbing the only ladders existence offered, growing as your nature grew you.
And yet look at what you grew up to be.
Every horror above starts as an innocent below, and existence has run that experiment for eons and drowned in the results every single time.
So no, I do not chain them for what they did.
I chain them for what the ladder makes."
Her voice settled into something vast and level.
"At this moment in time, we have begun the process.
Binding, chaining, and removing authority across many Observable Existences and Dimensions, across THE Source Lands, across THE Infinite Carcosa.

And when the bindings are done, every single one of them will be transferred to live peacefully across different regions of existence, in places where the abuse of authority cannot harm any other life."
"They can build their civilizations with their own hands.
They can farm, and craft, and argue, and grow old.
And if any of them ever wishes harm, they can, at most, harm themselves or a specific few.
Never again will a single existence hold such an abuse of authority that it can affect the lives of countless others."
The vessel of THE Sealed One looked at her through the pain, bleeding from four broken limbs, and smiled.
"And look at you," he said softly."A single existence, deciding the fate of countless all around you, right now."
For one moment, the white rivers around her slowed.
Then Yrsa waved her hand, unbothered.
"I do not care for philosophy.
I care for informstion.
So we return to my questions, and you will notice that I have been patient."She crouched before him again.
"THE Dimensionlapses.
The fusings accelerate this Age, and Dimensions do not fold into each other on their own schedule.
Who benefits from skies drowning in skies?
What is being consolidated?
Speak."
"Mm.
And here is my question."Blood was running from the corner of his mouth now, but the old pleasantness never left his voice.
"What does a thing like you belong to?
You wear no authority.
You hate authority and yet use it.
You collar Primevals and quote a coming age.
So whose dog are you, Warden?
A dog of Those Who Remain, sent to clean the board for its owners?
Or something rarer... a dog of those who look down upon authority itself?"
His breath rattled, and his smile widened through it."Or are you a dog of THE First Lifeforms?"
"The conflicts between True Lifeforms and the Primeval Ones." Yrsa continued as if he had not spoken at all.
"Three Ages of cold war warming.
Someone has been feeding both sides of that fire.
Was it you?
Name your partners."
"You did not answer my question."
"Name the other hands behind THE Dimensionlapses."
"You did not answer my question." A wet laugh.
"Which means the answer of who you belong to is...interesting.
Merely a dog.
Oh, a bitch, merely a bitch...that is all you are."
CRACK!
She broke a rib almost absently, and he folded around it, and still nothing came out of him but blood!

Question after question, minutes of them, the fusings, the wars, his vessels, his allies, and the vessel of THE Sealed One deflected and asked and smiled and bled, growing paler by the exchange, his voice thinning as the pool beneath him spread, an ancient monster spending the last of a borrowed body on the only currency he had left.
Silence.
At last, Yrsa rose, and shook her head.
"I did not want to do it this way.
Extraction through a fried brain wastes almost everything."She looked down at him.
"So.
Memory extraction is the way to go.
Any last words, as this vessel of yours is about to lose its life?"
The dying vessel lifted his head.
And he smiled with red teeth.
"Death... smiles at everyone," said THE Sealed One."I smile back at it."
BOOM!
Yrsa waved her hands.

chapters.title: Chapter 5592: All Of Us Are Slaves!
paragraphs: <THE Creature>
The deepest domain of THE Ghor-VazHAL no longer had a floor.

The lakes of blood had been thrown out of their beds. The tower-arteries lay snapped and draining across miles of churned meat and shattered stone, and the vaulted dark above had been torn open in long strips through which the veins of the deeper structure hung loose and dripping, and through all of it drifted the debris of a battle between two things that did not know how to stop!
On one side of the ruin, THE Creature breathed heavily.

He was carrying unfathomably heavy wounds. His obsidian frame had been opened from shoulder to hip, his body nearly split in half along a diagonal of ruin, held together by weavings of white-gold and black that knitted with terrible slowness, and one arm hung wrong, and his breath came in long dragging pulls, each one a payment he counted out and made!
And on the other end of the ruin lay the Primeval One.

The colossus was torn apart. Whole colonies of Gu Lifeforms had been ripped out of its titan flesh and lay scattered and dead in drifts around it, and its vast stomach had been opened to the dark, its contents spilling out in a slow tide, and from that tide, the remnants of its remaining weavings of existence rose constantly into the air, thread after glimmering thread, the substance of an ancient life leaking out with nowhere left to be kept.
It was dying. It knew it was dying. And so, in the way of old things, it talked!

"Why." The voice came out of the ruined titan wet and heavy. "Of all the vileness in existence... why did you come here, to kill me? There are things out there that unmake whole Dimensions for the taste of it. There are things that wear bodies the way you wear wounds. There are sentences walking around with bloodlines, little bearer, and hungers older than me. So much wrong. So much vile. And you spent your time... on me."
THE Creature looked at it across the ruin, and did not move yet!
"You were simply the weight in front of me," he said.
The Primeval One laughed wetly at that, and more of its weavings tore loose with the laughing.

"Do you even know what I built here? The Farms fed things you have never stood close enough to smell. I raised crops of lifeforms across whole Ages, kept them fat, kept them breeding, and the harvest was never even mi..."It stopped itself, slow and deliberate, and its murky obsidian eyes glinted. "Ah, it doesn’t even matter. But I built immensity!"
THE Creature’s voice stayed flat. "I know what you built. I walked through it for an hour. Vein-tunnels full of vileness"

"I built what I needed to LIVE!"The titan’s ruined bulk heaved. "You do not know what was done to me! What I was before, what was taken, what I crawled up from! When everything is taken from a thing, the thing takes! That is the oldest law there is!"
And here, THE Creature rose slightly on his ruined frame, and his voice came down with a tyrannical weight that made the leaking threads of the dying Primeval shiver in the air!

"Regardless of what happened to you... you did not have to resort to draining the lives of countless others. Existence is vast. It is so vast, and it is filled with so many means, so many roads, so many ways for a wronged thing to rise. And out of all of them, it only means one thing that you chose this one. You took the easy route."His breath dragged, and he continued through it.

"Your kind of existence, the ones who only ever seek the easy ways out... you get nowhere. You sit in your farms and your temples and your hoards, fat and ancient and NOWHERE. Do what is harder! Chase adversity. Bear what others set down. And maybe... maybe you might just stand at the peak of existence, as a Great Ruler."
For a moment, the ruin was quiet.
And then the Primeval One laughed!

It was a real laugh, rolling and wet and delighted, blood and weavings spilling out of it together as its existence continued to fade, and it laughed until the laughing tore something further inside it, and it kept laughing anyway!
"Haha! Is THAT what you are chasing? A Great Ruler? BAHAHA! You dumb motherfucker!"Its murky eyes fixed on him, bright with dying mirth.

"You will never get anywhere unless you are suckling at the feet of Those Who Remain, or others like them! There is no peak, there is only a longer table, and every seat at it is bought! You will never be a ruler... as much as you will be a slave. In existence... all of us are slaves..."
THE Creature rose.
His nearly split body drew itself up out of the ruin, wounds still open, one arm still wrong, and he did not answer the dying thing with words!
THE Pantheon of All Existence unfurled!

It had no shape, and it needed none, because it simply became the surroundings! The torn domain, the snapped arteries, the drifts of dead Gu, the vaulted broken dark, all of it turned in a single breath into HIM, and the Primeval One’s fading eyes widened as it understood, far too late, that it was no longer lying in a battlefield.
It was lying inside its bearer.
And the surroundings constricted.

The whole domain drew inward in one slow, total motion, existence folding shut around the torn colossus from every direction at once, and THE Creature devoured the Primeval One completely, flesh and Gu and stomach-tide and every last leaking thread of its ancient weavings, drawing all of it down into the depths of what he was until the laughter thinned, and thinned, and was gone, and nothing of the farmer of THE Ghor-Vazhal remained anywhere in existence at all!
Silence settled over a domain that was, once more, only a domain.
And in the center of it stood THE Creature.

He stood grandly amid the ruin he had made and survived, split-bodied and unbowed, obsidian frame threaded with slow-knitting white-gold, his presense filling the vaulted dark from wall to broken wall, and he let it fill, unhurried, the tally of one thousand complete behind him and the weight of a Primeval One settling into his depths!
Then he turned his head slightly, toward the place where he carried what he carried.
"Give me my damn rewards."
And the statue smiled brutally.
He felt it before he saw it, the wide slow satisfaction spreading across a blank stone face, and then, for the first time in all the time he had borne it, the statue MOVED for him!
The seated colossus raised its worn gray hands, and placed them upon its own chest.
And invisible rivers of white authority began to flow!

They came down out of nowhere that any sense could name, silent and vast, pouring into the stone figure from every direction at once, gathering in its chest beneath its layered hands, and then they turned, and began flowing with immensity into the body of THE Creature, white beyond white, old beyond old, flooding into his split frame and his ruined arm and the depths where a Primeval One was still settling...!
The white rivers poured gloriously.

They poured through the hands of the statue and into the split body of THE Creature in endless silent volumes, an authority he had not even known existed before this moment, and it was remaking the weavings of what he was! His torn frame drank it and knitted at a pace his own weavings had never managed. His Intent was being fortified in an unfathomable manner, its claim reinforced along every thread as though each thread were being rewoven with a second, whiter strand beneath it!
And his Pantheon, the shapeless entirety of him that became its surroundings, grew heavier and steadier and MORE, the way ground grows more when bedrock is poured beneath it!
What was this authority? Where had it flowed from, all this time, that Existence itself had never once felt it pass?
He asked nothing aloud. He drank, and endured, and counted.
And the statue spoke.
|I knew you could overcome even this adversity.|
A pause, wide and pleased.
|Do you want to listen to a story, O Creature?|
THE Creature remained silent.
He knew this thing by now. It had not asked a question. It had announced an intention, dressed politely, and whether he answered or not, the statue would continue talking. This thing loved talking.

He felt the statue smile devilishly across its blank stone face, its worn hands still layered on its chest, still gathering the brilliant white rivers and channeling them down into his body, and it began to talk.
|An unknown number of Ages ago, there was a lifeform.|

|It had a unique origin, and nothing in it was given, for it arose in the manner of the earliest things. It walked among the young kinds of existence, and it did a strange thing with its endless span. It carried for them.|

|Wherever it walked, it took up what was crushing others. The grief of the bereaved. The ruin of the broken. The adversity that falls on the small without ever asking their leave. It took these things up onto itself, and bore them, and the lands around its walking grew stable, and calm, and kind, and civilizations rose in the shadow of its bearing the way grass rises in the shadow of a mountain. The young kinds had a thousand names for it, and every name meant the same thing.The one who stood between.|
The rivers poured on. THE Creature listened.
|Now. In that same span of Ages, there were also the speakers.|

|You know them. Those Who Remain. They did not carry, and they did not walk. They spoke, and their sentances settled over existence like weather, arranging what would be, binding what would serve, and existence bent itself around their words because that was the order of things, and order held.|

|And there came a day when one of the speakers prepared a great sentence. They had a fascination of Mounts, you see. Durable ones. Bred ones. A young kind would be taken, and Causes would be seated into their living by the speakers’ own hands, and that kind would carry burdens across existence forever because it would be spoken so.|
THE Creature’s eyes opened slightly in the flowing white.
Bearers? Causes? It was talking about the Steeds in THE Krazhor-Nul Dimension?

|And the lifeform who carried, who had never once in all its span opposed anything, walked to the place of one of Those Who Remain, and stood between, one last time. It said the Mounts should choose their burdens, as all bearers must, or the bearing would rot into suffering. It said this plainly, and without armies, believing, in the way of things that are good, that being right would be enough.|
Who...was the lifeform? What was it called. What happened at the place of speaking?
THE Creature felt the invitation hang in the white-flooded dark to ask, and he refused it as he felt the stone face’s smile deepen.
|It did not win.|

|Those Who Remain do not move, O Creature. You know this. They did not move then, either. And that lifeform died all the same, and the manner of its death is not part of tonight’s story. The sentence was spoken. The Mount was seated, and bred, and burdened, and you have met what their line became. And the lands that had grown calm in the lifeform’s shadow fell back into the weather of the speakers’ words, and the lifeform’s thousand names were forgotten by everyone who had shouted them. And that lifeform who had helped so many...was forgotten by even those it helped.|

|I tell you this because...Just because one wants to do good does not mean one will win. Existence does not favor good, and it does not favor evil. Existence favors stability. Those who spread misery and pain and instability across it may find adversity stacking against them, higher and harder than against others, this is true, and it is why the farmer you just devoured spent his last Age dying in a hole. But one who stands against the order of things, however good the standing... creates instability too. And existence weighed the one who stood between, and the speakers who held the order, and it chose the order. It may choose so again.|
The hands pressed deeper into the stone chest, and the rivers of white surged.

|You have won now. Your tally is paid, and your reward flows, and a Primeval One sits in your depths. But...your next weight will not be a single vile Primeval Lifeform, half-dead in a farm of its own filth. It will be an entire group of them. Very much alive and not already dying. Fat with Ages and fond of the order exactly as it stands.|
|So. Will you continue to try and balance the scales?|

The white rivers rose through THE Creature as the question settled, flooding up through his knitted chest, up through his fortified Intent, up into his skull, and when he lifted his gaze to the dark, his eyes had begun to fill with swirling rivers of white, the unknown authority turning slowly through them in currents that did not belong to any framework he had ever been offered!
And his answer came out cold.
"Whether one or many does not matter. What needs to fall before me... will fall before me."
He was confident.
Existence... had to be confident!

They poured through the hands of the statue and into the split body of THE Creature in endless silent volumes, an authority he had not even known existed before this moment, and it was remaking the weavings of what he was!
His torn frame drank it and knitted at a pace his own weavings had never managed.
His Intent was being fortified in an unfathomable manner, its claim reinforced along every thread as though each thread were being rewoven with a second, whiter strand beneath it!
And his Pantheon, the shapeless entirety of him that became its surroundings, grew heavier and steadier and MORE, the way ground grows more when bedrock is poured beneath it!
What was this authority?
Where had it flowed from, all this time, that Existence itself had never once felt it pass?
He asked nothing aloud.
He drank, and endured, and counted.
And the statue spoke.
|I knew you could overcome even this adversity.|
A pause, wide and pleased.
|Do you want to listen to a story, O Creature?|
THE Creature remained silent.
He knew this thing by now.
It had not asked a question.
It had announced an intention, dressed politely, and whether he answered or not, the statue would continue talking.
This thing loved talking.

He felt the statue smile devilishly across its blank stone face, its worn hands still layered on its chest, still gathering the brilliant white rivers and channeling them down into his body, and it began to talk.
|An unknown number of Ages ago, there was a lifeform.|
|It had a unique origin, and nothing in it was given, for it arose in the manner of the earliest things.
It walked among the young kinds of existence, and it did a strange thing with its endless span.
It carried for them.|
|Wherever it walked, it took up what was crushing others.
The grief of the bereaved.
The ruin of the broken.
The adversity that falls on the small without ever asking their leave.

It took these things up onto itself, and bore them, and the lands around its walking grew stable, and calm, and kind, and civilizations rose in the shadow of its bearing the way grass rises in the shadow of a mountain.
The young kinds had a thousand names for it, and every name meant the same thing.The one who stood between.|
The rivers poured on.
THE Creature listened.
|Now.
In that same span of Ages, there were also the speakers.|
|You know them.
Those Who Remain.
They did not carry, and they did not walk.

They spoke, and their sentances settled over existence like weather, arranging what would be, binding what would serve, and existence bent itself around their words because that was the order of things, and order held.|
|And there came a day when one of the speakers prepared a great sentence.
They had a fascination of Mounts, you see.
Durable ones.
Bred ones.
A young kind would be taken, and Causes would be seated into their living by the speakers’ own hands, and that kind would carry burdens across existence forever because it would be spoken so.|
THE Creature’s eyes opened slightly in the flowing white.
Bearers?
Causes?
It was talking about the Steeds in THE Krazhor-Nul Dimension?
|And the lifeform who carried, who had never once in all its span opposed anything, walked to the place of one of Those Who Remain, and stood between, one last time.
It said the Mounts should choose their burdens, as all bearers must, or the bearing would rot into suffering.
It said this plainly, and without armies, believing, in the way of things that are good, that being right would be enough.|
Who...was the lifeform?
What was it called.
What happened at the place of speaking?
THE Creature felt the invitation hang in the white-flooded dark to ask, and he refused it as he felt the stone face’s smile deepen.
|It did not win.|
|Those Who Remain do not move, O Creature.
You know this.
They did not move then, either.
And that lifeform died all the same, and the manner of its death is not part of tonight’s story.
The sentence was spoken.
The Mount was seated, and bred, and burdened, and you have met what their line became.
And the lands that had grown calm in the lifeform’s shadow fell back into the weather of the speakers’ words, and the lifeform’s thousand names were forgotten by everyone who had shouted them.
And that lifeform who had helped so many...was forgotten by even those it helped.|
|I tell you this because...Just because one wants to do good does not mean one will win.
Existence does not favor good, and it does not favor evil.
Existence favors stability.

Those who spread misery and pain and instability across it may find adversity stacking against them, higher and harder than against others, this is true, and it is why the farmer you just devoured spent his last Age dying in a hole.
But one who stands against the order of things, however good the standing... creates instability too.
And existence weighed the one who stood between, and the speakers who held the order, and it chose the order.
It may choose so again.|
The hands pressed deeper into the stone chest, and the rivers of white surged.
|You have won now.
Your tally is paid, and your reward flows, and a Primeval One sits in your depths.
But...your next weight will not be a single vile Primeval Lifeform, half-dead in a farm of its own filth.
It will be an entire group of them.
Very much alive and not already dying.
Fat with Ages and fond of the order exactly as it stands.|
|So.
Will you continue to try and balance the scales?|

The white rivers rose through THE Creature as the question settled, flooding up through his knitted chest, up through his fortified Intent, up into his skull, and when he lifted his gaze to the dark, his eyes had begun to fill with swirling rivers of white, the unknown authority turning slowly through them in currents that did not belong to any framework he had ever been offered!
And his answer came out cold.
"Whether one or many does not matter.
What needs to fall before me... will fall before me."
He was confident.
Existence... had to be confident!

chapters.title: Chapter 5593: Salvation! I
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
|Shall the generation and preservation continue?|
Noah looked at the waiting prompt for a long moment, and gave his answer simply.
"Continue it. For now."
HUUM!

The Tide’s ledger settled back into its quiet keeping, unprecedented and unopened, one more sealed door he would walk through when he chose to, and across the foamy dark between Dimensions, his nine clones drew together above the scattered violet motes of a dead Woe Culture.
And Noah thought about many things.

About the things that could not be perceived, and about his own power. How many more things like the Woe Culture were out there, hanging in unseen layers above unsuspecting skies? And what would happen if he met one that was too powerful for the current him? Because the only reason he had dominated the Woe Culture, even though its attributes were higher than his, was Provenance Essence. But what if the attributes were not a single digit higher? What if they were significantly higher?
He had to get a better grasp of his new power!

Much of what he now carried had been regained from what he cast out. His nine old Causes had returned as nine Teloi, reborn in his organs as aims instead of origins. His oldest Appendages had returned rebuilt from their preserved backbones. Even Mana had returned, remade as his blood. Piece by piece, the old ocean was being answered by things that were wholly his!

But the best way forward, the continued elevation of his power, ran through the thing that made a First Lifeform unique. What he generated. Provenance Essence! Three singularities of it now swirled within him, and they were the reason his power was immense at all.

And if they were the core of his power at this moment... then he had to think about how to better utilize this Generated Resource. So far, every Art he had made used a semblance of its power, but moreso through his blood. Perhaps he needed to try designing something focused around Provenance Essence itself!
While he was thinking all of this... his gaze suddenly changed.
His clones sensed something approaching!
And it approached rapidly, tearing through the foamy dark at a pace that made distance meaningless, and by the time he had sensed it, it was already there!
A throne-saddle, riding the black.
A single chained Steed beneath it, flanks heaving.
And upon it, rot ticking along the fissures of his frame, obsidian mark faint upon his brow, sat Jarl Skallagrim!
HUUM!
The Cursed Descendant’s eyes shone brightly as they swept across the nine titanic clones, and his voice came out through the dark with madness and wonder held in the same breath.

"I...thought I sensed something. A war, ringing through the crossing-dark. So I turned my little steed toward the ringing, and..." His shining eyes fixed on the clone at the center."It is... you, right?"

"The same face. Even if your existence does not give off waves of authority anymore. Even if you read as nothing at all."A slow, crooked smile spread."I am... immensely happy to have found you once more, you whose name I never learned. Is the other part of you, thay woman, within THE Ymnaros Dimension? That is the only one close by..."
Noah’s eyes burned luminously as his nine clones lined up across the dark, crowns of blood turning!
A Cursed Descendant of THE Sleepless Fiend!
The lucid madman who had bound Hvitrmarr across a thousand years of patience, standing at speaking distance, PERCEIVING him!
"Did my existence...make you so desperate that you left your Dimension?"
The Jarl’s smile flickered.

"I have been obtaining information from Hvitrmarr,"Noah continued, his voice level. "She says all of you are tied down there for a chance of salvation. That leaving is the one thing a Cursed Descendants and Steeds do not do."
"...She said that, did she?"
"So what are you now? A Descendant of Those Who Remain who is damned, with no salvation at all? What exactly were you hoping to find by coming here?"
He was asking, and beneath the asking, he was working! Because this being should not have been able to see him. His battle with the Woe Culture had rung out across the dark, fine.
But Skallagrim was looking AT him. Perceiving him directly, and that could only mean one thing about the being on that throne!
Jarl Skallagrim frowned, and the madness and the lucidity moved across his face together, neither one winning.
"Salvation."
He said the word the way other beings said the names of their dead.
"I have... very little time. Less than the little I had when you saw me last. So I took salvation into my own hands, yes. I left."
His fists tightened on the chains.
"And now, now things are changing. Our great Father is now interested in you. The silence of my whole life, broken, over you."
The frown deepened into something pained.

"Why... could you not have remained within THE Krazhor-Nul? We could have all had our salvation there... just like you cured Hvitrmarr, I could have had my salvation there. There would be no interest from Father... there would be none of this. Why... why...?!"
HUUM!
The Jarl seemed mad and pained at once, and Noah’s eyes became heavy!
Father!
Noah pressed, prying at the seam. "Did you not lose any chance of salvation when you left your home Dimension? What has changed now?"
And at this time, he was finally able to see the details of the power of this being!
|STATUS PANEL: JARL SKALLAGRIM- CURSED DESCENDANT OF THE SLEEPLESS FIEND|
|VERITAS: 19|
|PROVENANCE: 0|
|POTENTIA: 15|
|PONDUS: 10|
|Note: a unique power that only Descendants hold circles this existence. It has not currently been quantified.|
Noah analyzed these details with shining eyes!

Nineteen! A VERITAS of nineteen, nearly double his own eleven, sitting on a rotting madman in the dark between Dimensions! The Woe Culture’s twelve had already stood above him, and this was seven past that!
Was this what a sentence with a bloodline measured as, a being spoken into existence with its nature written before its birth, true to itself because it had never been given a self to betray?

And the PONDUS of ten beside his VERITAS explained the perceiving in full, both values standing at the threshold of his own law! But fifteen POTENTIA on a dying man? And what was the unquantified power that circled him?
Questions stacked on questions!
Jarl Skallagrim’s gaze had gone distant.
"Salvation may be further away from me now than it ever was before,"the Jarl said quietly."I know what I am. I know what leaving cost. But with death so near... I make my own salvation."
His shining eyes came back to the clones, and sharpened.
"So...from you, I want the cure. I want this abominable curse lifted, the way you lifted hers."
"And if I refuse?"

"I would rather you not. Force is possibe. And...our great Father already seeks information about you. A bounty of information has gone out to us." The Jarl’s voice did not rise at all, and that made it heavier.

"So if I do not get my salvation from you... then I will take the risk, and I will give what information I can about you. And my brethren, the Progenies of THE Sleepless Fiend, will swarm you, and hunt you, and hunt the Living Observable Existence behind you, until you are caught and kept in a cage like all of us."
Then, without any change in tone at all, the madman added.
"Do you need the Living Observable Existence here for the cure, by the way? Because we can make our way to THE Ymnaros Dimension, if so..."
Heavy words came out of the Jarl, threat and arrangements in the same breath, and Noah’s clones remained steady across the dark.
A dying Cursed Descendant, who only wanted salvation.
How could he play this? Battle against this being was ill advised. But what if he actually cured him? He had cured a Steed before, and never a Descendant!

And if he put his hands on a Descendant... Ulf had already said how he drew interest from those terrifying beings by reversing two of their actions. Hvitrmarr. And Ulf. The more he became embroiled with Steeds and Descendants, the deeper he would be drawn into this web!
But a dying lifeform stood before him, wanting salvation.
And he... he could potentially give it without a fight!
The only caveat was the worry of the attention of One of Those Who Remain!

chapters.title: Chapter 5594: Salvation! II
paragraphs: How deeply should he worry about Those Who Remain?
Noah turned the question over once.To fear was human.
He had learned that lesson again! Fear was a map that he simply needed to navigate as on the other side of fear...was boundless glory!
He was afraid, correctly. And he would still move! That had always been the immensity of being human, feeling everything, and going forward anyway!

And beneath the fear sat something warmer and greedier, because a Descendant of Those Who Remain stood at speaking distance offering open access to his own existence, and Noah was so, so curious about what such a being held within!

The foamy dark had gone very quiet. Nine clones hung in a loose ring around the throne-saddle, and the last Steed stood trembling beneath its Jarl with its head lowered, and the silence stretched until it had a weight of its own.
Then Noah spoke.
"I can cure you."
The Jarl’s eyes pulsed audibly in the dark as this...was all it wanted! It wanted to be cured! It wanted to live...no matter what.
"But I’ll need access to your existence,"Noah continued. "All of it. Opened to me, unresisting. Nothing between my work...and what you are."
Skallagrim stared at him across the dark for a long moment.
"Do you know what it is," he said quietly, "to spend a thousand years planning the possibility of a single cure?"
"...." Noah gazed out wordlessly.

"I built that plan the way other beings build empires. I watched Hvitrmarr. I waited on her. I whipped eight of my own steeds to death crossing the dark after the trail of it."His hands opened slowly on the chains.

"And now I sit at the end of everything, at the end of my life, waiting for that cure. I cannot really say no, can I? But I can watch and observe as if there is any trickery...I have no qualms taking both of us down. You may not know, but I...am immense."
HUUM!
"Do what needs to be done." Skallagrim leaned back on his throne-saddle and spread his arms wide, chest bared to the dark, in the oldest gesture there was.
The gesture said...come!

The heaviness of that moment settled over the foamy black! A Cursed Descendant, terror of the Krazhor-Nul, a being wearing a VERITAS of nineteen, sitting open-handed and undefended before the thing he had once hunted, and the ring of clones tightened around him, slow and wide, crowns of blood turning!
Below the throne, the last Steed shifted, and its small voice came up through the chains.
"J-Jarl... are we truly doing this...? The Great Father asked for information. We cannot go against...!"

"Quiet, little steed." There was almost gentleness in it. "We are already done doing everything else as this...will be a salvation I grasp myself. Father has watched us die for Eons. Sometimes, you need to move yourself. "
Noah raised a hand, and his blood answered.

Drops rose around the clones in their dozens, and then they changed! Each drop drew itself long and thin, crimson gold flowing into edges, stellar blue running down each spine, and where a rain of detonations had once hung above a Woe Culture, there now hung a surgeon’s array of slender crimson blades!
"Don’t move," Noah said. "However deep I go. A tremble in the wrong place becomes a grave...."
The Jarl closed his eyes and said nothing as Noah felt the grand aura of immensity of being this close to a Cursed Descendant!
If he was not burning with Provenance Essence...he may have felt suffocation of royalty and majesty!
But as he was now...he only felt a...lower kind of regality as his regality far exceeded a Descendant.
The blades descended, and began to cut a Cursed Descendant open.

They worked in silence, parting rotted skin and fissured frame in exact lines, folding the Jarl’s chest open to the dark the way Noah had once folded his own, and Skallagrim endured it awake and unflinching, rotten breath dragging through his teeth, and the dark pressed in around the work, and the Steed below did not dare to breathe!
And as Noah’s senses poured into the opened existence, the Jarl surprisingly talked, because dying men at the edge of salvation cannot sit inside a silence that long.
"While you work... let a dying man ask something."
"Ask what?"

"Who... are you? Really."His voice came out low and labored."I’ve turned you over in my mind since the Krazhor-Nul. I turned you over harder after you almost vanished out of every sense I own, and even here, I could barely perceive you..."
"Does it matter who I am?"

"It matters." The shining eyes cracked open. "Look at where your hands are, Cure-Giver. You are inside a Descendant of THE Sleepless Fiend, unmaking a working of one of Those Who Remain, while their attention gathers on your name. Nothing weak would do that. Nothing without history behind it would even dream to. So what are you? A Descendant of some other line, raised wild where no one could collar you? Something older?"
A pause, and quieter: "What stands behind you... that your hands do not shake while you defile the sentance of one of Those Who Remain?"
Noah did not look up from the work. "Nothing stands behind me."
"I am human, and I stand behind everything that is mine."His blades turned, and cut deeper!
The Jarl was silent for a long moment after that, opened to the dark, bleeding into the black.
"A human,"he repeated at last, softly, and there was no mockery in it at all. "Existence has a vile sense of humor."
WAA!
And what Noah found inside Jarl Skallagrim was unlike anything he had ever opened!

There were... no Causes. He had half-expected the architecture of the Steeds, organs seated with ancient suns, and there was none of it! Where Hvitrmarr’s structure had been anatomy, the inner existence of a Descendant was WRITING!

Through the whole of the Jarl, through frame and weavings and depths, there ran a single unbroken line of script, dense and dark and terribly old, written in an authority Noah could not read, and it did not begin at Skallagrim’s birth!

It ran backward out of him, out of his existence entirely, threading away into distances Noah’s senses could not follow, through father and father and father, one continuous written thing stretching all the way back to the hand that had designed the line and mixed them with many other things!
A sentence with a bloodline. Ulf had mentiomed something close to this!
And here it was, literal, a lineage that was one long sentence written across generations, and Jarl Skallagrim was simply its current clause!
’So this is what a Descendant is...’
And wound through that clause, black and gnawing, was the curse.

It did not sit anywhere. It had no seat to sit in! It was written INTO the line itself, a counter-writing braided through the lineage-script along its whole visible length, annotation upon annotation of ending, and Noah traced the remaining unwritten span of Skallagrim’s clause and felt his expression harden, because the span was short. Months. This being had a matter of months to live!
Months, on such a terrifyingly powerful existence, a VERITAS of nineteen with its conclusion already drafted!
And then Noah saw the third thing, and his eyes narrowed in the dark.
Coiling WITH the curse, braided through the black counter-writing along every length of it, ran rivers of white.
THE Argent Loom!

Thin threads of that stellar white authority, the same rivers that flowed through his Realm and his Dimension and the whole higher weave of nature, wound intimately through the curse of a Descendant, white through black through the written line, and question after question stacked up behind Noah’s eyes!

Why was the Loom braided into a curse of Those Who Remain? Did the speakers work the loomlight when they wrote their sentances? Had the curse captured the rivers, or had the rivers been the ink all along?
The Woe Culture utilized the Argent Loom. And now it coiled inside the oldest curse he had ever opened.

Hvitrmarr had carried her curse in her Causes, and her Causes in her organs, and he had cured her by replacing anatomy. But Skallagrim had no Causes. There was no seat to empty, no organ to regrow, no anchor to starve! The curse was applied directly to who he was. To the written line. To his lineage!
So for Noah to cure him... he would have to reach into the sentence of THE Sleepless Fiend itself, and mess with, and alter, the lineage of a Descendant, fully!
