chapters.title: Chapter 5612: Chain Them! II
paragraphs: <Warden Yrsa>
Warden Yrsa came into the crossing-dark outside THE Ymnaros.
The white rivers opened behind her, and her forces came through.

They came in silence as dozens of them poured out of the loomlight, and every one of them was shrouded head to toe in white cloth that left nothing of a face or a frame to read, their wrappings drawn tight and bound at the wrists and the throat, and around each shrouded figure, rivers of THE Argent Loom turned slowly in orbit!

Not one of them emanated a thread of authority as they fanned out toward the fused Dimension! Not an Intent among them. Not an ounce of Source, not a breath of Infinity, and their presense registered nowhere at all as they went!
Yrsa watched them deploy.
A single one of them was equivalent to a weak Primeval Lifeform.

One shrouded servant, wrapped and bound and silent, carried enough refined force to end the kind of ancient thing that entire Dimensions built religions around, and she had brought dozens of them, and they moved in units and obeyed without a sound! Existence outside these folds had no records of them, and existence would learn of them one incursion at a time!
And her own power exceeded any common Primeval One.

She did not dwell on it. She had stood before Primeval Lifeforms fat with Ages, things that had grazed on Dimensions since before the frameworks were named, and she had walked out of those meetings and they had not.

Below and ahead, THE Ymnaros went about its afternoon! Countless lifeforms moving through Observable Existences and a fused Dimension, and above them, the guardians of this Dimension stood at their posts and felt nothing coming!
Yrsa looked at all of it, and she thought about the weavings of the unworthy.
Authority was not evil. Authority was a hammer that existence handed out at random to whoever climbed the right ladder fast enough, and the trouble was never the hammer!

The trouble was that existence handed it to ANYONE, and then walked away, and never once came back to check what was being built with it! THE Sealed One had been handed a hammer and had ground an entire Age of his own children, and he was not the exception, he was simply the example everyone remembered. There were many like him.
Not one of them had been worthy of what they held.
"Positions," Yrsa said.
The shrouded ones reported across the loomlight in a flat overlapping chorus.
|The dragon.|
|The blindfolded one.|
|The scholar.|
|The strongest of the ones with no authority.|
|The pledged beneath them.|
"The Descendant outside is mine," she said. "Nobody touches him but me. Chains ready. Cages ready. Nothing sequential."
|Understood.|

She raised her hand, and the thing in it was a plain gray cylinder without a single mark on it, and thread-fine lines of white ran through its surface the way they ran through every collar her order had ever closed.
A Dimensional Inhibitor.
One second. Barely less. And then nothing from it for a long while after, because there were not many of these in all of existence and each one was worth more than a thousand Primeval Ones!
"Sweep," said Warden Yrsa.
And she broke the cylinder.
HUUM!
A silent light wept across everything like the cry of existence itself being disallowed to express itself!
And...
Authority died across THE Ymnaros!

It went out everywhere at once, a single silent second in which every ladder in the Dimension simply stopped existing, and nothing struck anyone, and nothing burned, and nothing was even touched! Things were simply subtracted! Intents guttered as Pantheons of Infinite Lifeforms folded, and the crimson gold weavings threaded through the key figures of this domain went dark from the sky down to the soil!
And her forces MOVED!
Hvitrmarr was flying the northern side of the fused Dimension filled with Infinite Lifeforms, enjoying her freedom, when the sky went quiet.
The White Steed, THE Blood Duke, vampiric crimson beneath white with her red gold wings spread across gigaparsecs of new territory, felt her nine transforming organs stop answering her instsntly!
Every single one of them went silent inside her body as her wings kept beating out of nothing but muscle and habit!
She fell.

A being who had carried burdens across three thousand years of chains dropped out of the northern sky and struck the ground hard enough to crack it for miles, and she smashed into shocked clusters of Infinite Lifeforms that were turned to pulp by her weight alone as none had any authority at this point!
Four shrouded figures came down on top of her.

They climbed her. White wrappings moved up her flanks and across her spine as the Loom-rivers around them bent down and pinned her wings flat to the stone, and when her wings strained against the pinning, the shrouded ones simply pressed harder, folding the great red gold spans backward at angles wings were never made to hold, and Hvitrmarr screamed in pain!

One of them walked the length of her neck with a gray band held open in both hands. She thrashed. She tore gorges through the ground with claws that were only claws now, and another shrouded one stepped onto the side of her head and stood there, its full Primeval-grade weight pressing her jaw into the broken stone, holding her skull utterly still no matter how she heaved beneath it, and the band closed anyway!
CLICK!
And then the chains came.

Loomlight poured off the shrouded ones in ropes as they wound them around her legs and her wings and her jaws, hardening as they wrapped, and they wound her jaws shut, muzzling an ancient queen mid-scream, and her voice broke off into a strangled sound through bound teeth, and her ancient existence read to every sense in existence as... a very large animal being tied down by farmhands!
"...Mmh! MMMH!"
She was still trying to say something through the muzzle.
Not again. Not again!
She did not want to be chained again!

They dragged her- two shrouded ones took the chains at her legs and hauled her across the ground on her side, her white flank grinding through the gorges her own claws had torn, and above the northern sky, something began to appear!

It came out of nothing in a grinding of dull gray metal, a cubical cage of that same seamless metal, wide enough to hold a dragon, and then another beside it, and another above that, stacking themselves into the air of a Dimension that had been free for hours!
They hauled her up to the first one, and they THREW her in!

Three thousand years of chains, hours of sky, and a being who had broken her own bindings through pure conserved will was thrown in without a shred of care, cargo and nothing more, striking the far wall hard enough to ring the whole cage, and the door ground shut on her before she had stopped sliding!
Inside it, bound and muzzled, THE Blood Duke shook in pain as she tried to scream...and was unable to.

The last Laestrygonian had been standing among Humans, as he often did now, letting the children stare at the blindfold of crimson gold hands across his face, and the moment the sweep landed, the hands went dark and dead and the great eye behind them shut for the first time.
He stood there in the street with his blindfold gone lifeless, and he understood immediately what had been done to him as he sought to move!
Three shrouded figures walked out of the crowd toward him at speeds his current existence could not follow, because all authority became inhibited and nullified... he was not able to do a thing!
But he could still move his body, and so the last Laestrygonian did the only thing left to him.
He stepped in front of the children.
He spread his arms across a street full of small staring faces, a being with a dead blindfold shielding Humans with nothing but his own frame, and the shrouded ones did not slow down for any of it!

They came through the crowd in straight lines, and the crowd was simply IN the lines! Their movements and authority trampled hundreds of nearby Humans to bloody pulp, bodies that had been laughing in a market street one breath ago crushed beneath wrappings that never once looked down, and Damodred ROARED, a sound no one in this citadel had ever heard from him, and threw himself at the nearest shrouded figure with his bare hands!
His fists struck a thing equivalent to a weak Primeval Lifeform, and his authority was gone, and the shrouded figure did not even sway.

They put the band on him in the middle of the screaming street, and they were not gentle about a single motion of it! One shrouded hand gripped the back of his neck and bent him, forcing the last Laestrygonian a murdered race down over the bodies of the Humans he had failed to shield, holding him folded there while the band clicked shut, and then the loomlight ropes went around his wrists and his elbows and his knees, cinched tight enough to cut, and they dragged him upward off the ground by the rope at his wrists, hanging, and a second cage ground into existence above the citadel and took him in the same way the first had taken the dragon!
Thrown. Rung against the far wall. Sealed.
And below, many Humans and some Superpowered Lifeforms stood in a street painted with their own people, and watched their new protector hang and vanish into a metal box in the sky.
In another direction.
Anaximander did not resist as he seemed to have sensed something in the last possible moment.
He watched Axon approach with the band, and he made no attempt to leave.
The band closed around the neck of a being no framework had ever managed to file.
And nothing happened.
Axon’s halos stopped turning.

Because the collar sat there at the scholar’s throat, seamless and sealed and doing absolutely nothing at all, and Anaximander looked down at it, and then he looked up, and there was nothing scholarly left in his face! Cold anger sat there instead.
And around him, the skies filled with weight!

They came from every direction at once. Ianthe Kallias landed on the stone beside him, and old Peleus came, and dozens more, many Superpowered Lifeforms of THE Ymnaros arriving as some of them were collared. And every one of them exactly as strong as they had been an hour ago!
"Were these collars... supposed to do something?" Anaximander said coldly.
And he reached up, took hold of the band at his throat with both hands, and tore it apart!
CRACK!
The pieces fell.
Anaximander stepped forward and cracked his knuckles as surrounding existence began to shake!
And gigaparsecs out, in the crossing-dark beyond the fused Dimension, Warden Yrsa went to collect the Descendant.

She found Jarl Skallagrim on his feet with his last Steed beside him, both of them stripped by the sweep, his crimson gold seas guttered and his fissures gone dim, and she walked toward them across the black with two gray bands in her hands and no hurry in her at all.
The Steed she took first.

It shrieked and tried to bolt, and one loomlight rope caught its neck and folded its legs beneath it mid-stride so that it crashed chin-first into the dark, and Warden Yrsa walked over to it, and set her boot on its neck, and closed the band around its throat with the ease of a keeper closing a gate!
CLICK!

Chains wound over it, cinched down until the little Steed could not raise its head, and it lay pinned in the dark and shook, uncursed and uncollared for barely a few hours of its existence, and collared again now, and its eyes rolled toward Skallagrim the whole time, asking him for something he could not give!
Then she turned to the Descendant, and she pressed the second band to his throat, and it began to close.
And it stopped halfway!
Because the shroud had come out!

THE Thousand Deaths I Do Not Owe billowed out of Skallagrim’s fissures in ragged dark crimson gold, every death that had ever been written into his clause and was now unpaid, and it drove itself into the closing band and jammed there, wedging the gray metal open a finger’s width from sealing!

The collar was still winning, closing by slow increments as the shroud thinned, and the Blood Sovereign’s arms shook as he held the thing off his own throat with a power that should have been switched off entirely!
Half bound. Half free!
Yrsa stopped, and she watched it for a long moment.
"Hm."
She tilted her head as she studied the wedged band.
"This is definitely a first. But I knew a Descendant would be troublesome..."
Skallagrim’s shroud thinned another fraction, and he dragged it back up with a roar!
"So." Yrsa clasped her hands.

And she looked past him at the Dimension behind his shoulder, where cages were still grinding into existence in the sky above a citadel, and a dragon lay muzzled and chained in the first of them, and a Laestrygonian hung bound in the second above a street of pulped Humans, and the only things still standing in that whole domain were beings who could not be collared and a scholar who had torn her work apart with his hands!
"What now?"
Skallagrim said nothing. His arms shook, and his crimson gold eyes moved once, past her, to the little Steed pinned under chains in the dark, and then back to her.

"Every powerful being in THE Ymnaros with authority to take has been taken. Your Steed is on the ground at my feet. And you are holding my band open with your own sheer will, which is magnificent, and which changes nothing at all."
Her hand rose, and settled on the wedged gray metal at his throat.
"So call forth your Master, you unruly motherfucker."
As she said such words, she used her power to forcefully close the Inhibitor around Skallagrim’s neck!

chapters.title: Chapter 5613: Accountable!
paragraphs: <Warden Yrsa>
An existence that gave THE Sealed One problems was not to be underestimated.
Yrsa held that thought at the center of everything as her hand pressed the wedged band.

Whatever this Blood-Crowned One was, a vessel of the oldest deceiver in existence had walked away from him, and things that made THE Sealed One walk away were things you learned about before you stood in front of them!
She needed knowledge. She had every advantage at this exact moment, and advantages were not things you saved for later!
So she moved, within spans of nanoseconds, while the capability of the Dimensional Inhibitor still held its subtraction over everything it had swept!

She could not do it to the Descendant as he was special. But she did not have the time to obtain information properly, and she did not need to, because information was lying right there in the dark, pinned under chains.
The steed.

It was now just a beast of flesh and bones! No authority. No curse. No frameworks, no ladders, nothing left in it that existence would even bother to name, and its brain held its memories and informstion all the same, so...
Warden Yrsa put her hand on the head of the fearful steed, ruthlessly, without a single word!
And she extracted.

Her power poured down through her palm into a skull that had nothing left to answer with, and the little steed’s whole body seized against its chains as its eyes flew wide, and it screamed, and no sound came out! Its jaws strained against the loomlight bindings in total silence as its memories were dragged up and out through the tearing, hours and years and a thousand cursed years hauled backward through flesh that was only flesh, and blood began to leak from its eyes, running down its face in thin dark lines as its silent scream went on and on!
Skallagrim’s roar shook the crossing-dark!
He heaved against the half-closed band with everything in him, his shroud flaring ragged, and the steed’s rolling eyes found him one last time through the blood!
And then...
BOOM!
Its head could not withstand the authority tearing across its existence!

The skull of that glorious steed burst apart in the dark, and the silent scream ended, and its entire existence simply ceased, every thread of it going out at once, and what lay pinned beneath the chains was a lifeless corpse that had been uncursed, and free, for less than a single day of its long and obedient life!
And Warden Yrsa breathed in.
Her eyes, pale and unmoved through many collarings, showed tremendous surprise!

Because the memories were in her now, hours of them, and what they held was... more than she had reckoned for! Far more! Her mind ran through them within nanoseconds, and her conclusions rearranged themselves, and she did not waste a single one of those nanoseconds standing still!
She moved.
Warden Yrsa appeared instantly behind Skallagrim, and her hands waved once!
HUUM!

Hundreds of radiant white swords manifested out of the loomlight, blades woven purely from THE Argent Loom, and they poured into orbit around the rageful figure of the Descendant, circling him in layered rings, and every single one of them came to rest a single millimeter from his skin! Points at his throat, his spine, his eyes, his fissures, hundreds of terrifying weapons of terrifying authority holding at a millimeter, so that any motion from anything, anywhere, would see them pierce him in but an instant!
Because existence outside the Dimension behind them had begun to tremble and shake!

Even without turning, Yrsa sensed the immense pressure that had arrived, pressure that had no business existing inside a region her Inhibitor had swept, and she turned her head calmly and gazed at what stood in the crossing-dark!
A manifestation of the Blood-Crowned One!

Crimson gold, crowned in blood, floating in the black with stellar light rolling off his frame in slow waves, and he had not just appeared here! Across her senses, similar manifestations were appearing in various areas of THE Ymnaros Dimension, above the citadel, over the northern skies, before the cages themselves!
But it did not matter.

She had already sent her commands within those same nanoseconds, to Axon, to the shrouded units, to every position her order held: utilize the prisoners. The chained and the collared and the caged were no longer captives now, they were leverage, placed exactly where they needed to be to control the flow of whatever battle would be commencing!
Warden Yrsa breathed out, and she looked ahead.

The manifestation before her was one of his clones, she knew that much from the dead steed’s memories, and his entire expression was unfathomably cold and rageful! Crimson gold eyes with singularities turning in their depths bore down on her with a weight that surprised her, his gaze moving once across the corpse of the steed, once across the hundreds of blades holding a millimeter from Skallagrim’s skin, and back to her!
And Yrsa was unfazed even as her existence pulsed as she felt like she was being looked at by something ancient! Haha, just who was this fucker to make her feel like this?
She shook her head slowly, and when she spoke, her voice was as calm and plain as it had been all afternoon.
"What an arrogant and unique piece of work you are."She glanced at the wedged band on Skallagrim’s throat. "Healing the curse of Steeds and cursed Descendants? Sheesh."
The dark trembled around his silence.

"I see you are angry. But it is nice to meet you."She tilted her head. "From the memories of that sad steed that unfortunately died after the memory extraction... I see you have been busy since curing Hvitrmarr and coming here. You even went as far as to cure a cursed Descendant. To give something salvation... when it was not your place to do so..."
"Who knows what more you would have done if I had not come along?"
The manifestation’s rage pressed against the crossing-dark, and still he did not move!
"But seeing you pause in rage there, you seem to already grasp the situation at hand."Yrsa raised one finger, and every blade in orbit brightened.

"Any move from you means this cursed Descendant, well... not cursed anymore... it means that this Descendant, and that dragon inside the Dimension, and all the others that my people have shackled and bound and inhibited... will die."
"So I advise you not to make a move."
The blades turned slowly at their millimeter, and Skallagrim’s shroud flickered between them, and his crimson gold eyes burned at her back with something that had no words in any tongue!

"I will even go as far as to say I don’t give a damn about this Descendant. Or the steed inside. Or that ugly looking thing with severed hands on its head." She said it all evenly, without a shred of heat. "If you just bring your body here... I can swap their freedom for yours. After all, they are merely followers. You are the leader."
Warden Yrsa clasped her hands behind her back, and looked into the cold rage of the Blood-Crowned One, and finished plainly.
"It is always those who lead that need to be held accountable. And I wanna hold you accountable, O Cure-Giver. O Blood-Crowned One."
Her pale eyes were very steady.
"I want... to hold you accountable."
HUUM!

Hundreds of radiant white swords manifested out of the loomlight, blades woven purely from THE Argent Loom, and they poured into orbit around the rageful figure of the Descendant, circling him in layered rings, and every single one of them came to rest a single millimeter from his skin!

Points at his throat, his spine, his eyes, his fissures, hundreds of terrifying weapons of terrifying authority holding at a millimeter, so that any motion from anything, anywhere, would see them pierce him in but an instant!
Because existence outside the Dimension behind them had begun to tremble and shake!

Even without turning, Yrsa sensed the immense pressure that had arrived, pressure that had no business existing inside a region her Inhibitor had swept, and she turned her head calmly and gazed at what stood in the crossing-dark!
A manifestation of the Blood-Crowned One!
Crimson gold, crowned in blood, floating in the black with stellar light rolling off his frame in slow waves, and he had not just appeared here!
Across her senses, similar manifestations were appearing in various areas of THE Ymnaros Dimension, above the citadel, over the northern skies, before the cages themselves!
But it did not matter.
She had already sent her commands within those same nanoseconds, to Axon, to the shrouded units, to every position her order held: utilize the prisoners.
The chained and the collared and the caged were no longer captives now, they were leverage, placed exactly where they needed to be to control the flow of whatever battle would be commencing!
Warden Yrsa breathed out, and she looked ahead.
The manifestation before her was one of his clones, she knew that much from the dead steed’s memories, and his entire expression was unfathomably cold and rageful!

Crimson gold eyes with singularities turning in their depths bore down on her with a weight that surprised her, his gaze moving once across the corpse of the steed, once across the hundreds of blades holding a millimeter from Skallagrim’s skin, and back to her!
And Yrsa was unfazed even as her existence pulsed as she felt like she was being looked at by something ancient!
Haha, just who was this fucker to make her feel like this?
She shook her head slowly, and when she spoke, her voice was as calm and plain as it had been all afternoon.
"What an arrogant and unique piece of work you are."She glanced at the wedged band on Skallagrim’s throat.
"Healing the curse of Steeds and cursed Descendants?
Sheesh."
The dark trembled around his silence.
"I see you are angry.
But it is nice to meet you."She tilted her head.
"From the memories of that sad steed that unfortunately died after the memory extraction...
I see you have been busy since curing Hvitrmarr and coming here.
You even went as far as to cure a cursed Descendant.
To give something salvation... when it was not your place to do so..."
"Who knows what more you would have done if I had not come along?"
The manifestation’s rage pressed against the crossing-dark, and still he did not move!
"But seeing you pause in rage there, you seem to already grasp the situation at hand."Yrsa raised one finger, and every blade in orbit brightened.

"Any move from you means this cursed Descendant, well... not cursed anymore... it means that this Descendant, and that dragon inside the Dimension, and all the others that my people have shackled and bound and inhibited... will die."
"So I advise you not to make a move."
The blades turned slowly at their millimeter, and Skallagrim’s shroud flickered between them, and his crimson gold eyes burned at her back with something that had no words in any tongue!
"I will even go as far as to say I don’t give a damn about this Descendant.
Or the steed inside.
Or that ugly looking thing with severed hands on its head." She said it all evenly, without a shred of heat.
"If you just bring your body here...
I can swap their freedom for yours.
After all, they are merely followers.
You are the leader."
Warden Yrsa clasped her hands behind her back, and looked into the cold rage of the Blood-Crowned One, and finished plainly.
"It is always those who lead that need to be held accountable.
And I wanna hold you accountable, O Cure-Giver.
O Blood-Crowned One."
Her pale eyes were very steady.
"I want... to hold you accountable."
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5614: Mistakes!
paragraphs: <Existential Interlude- Mistakes>
Nobody knows how long ago it was.
The record itself does not claim a time. It only claims that it happened, in the age when Those Who Remain still spoke often, and existence was still young enough to listen closely.
One of Those Who Remain had many Descendants.
His name is not written as the record calls him only the Father, and it calls his youngest Descendant Alvarr, and it says that Alvarr was born restless.
One day, Alvarr came before the Father and said, "Father, I wish to prove myself to you. Give me a quest."
The Father considered him for a long time. Then he said:
"Go out into existence, and bring me back a thing I do not have."
Alvarr bowed, and left that same instant!
This was the first mistake, and it was the mistake of haste.

Alvarr crossed a hundred Dimensions before it occured to him that he had never asked what the thing was. What did his Father lack? What could a being lack, when existence agreed with almost every one of his words? He did not know! He had been so eager to begin that he had run past the beginning entirely, and now an Age had been spent, and all of it was wandering!

He returned to his Father empty handed and ashamed, and he waited to be punished, and he waited a long time as his father was entertaining himself with one of THE First Lifeforms at that time for a whole millennium.
After waiting for his punishment in that millennium...
The Father did not punish him.

"Why would I punish a teacher?"the Father said. "Your mistake has just taught you what nothing else could have. You mistook motion for progress. All the living do this once. Most of them do it forever. Now you will not. Go again."
The second mistake was the mistake of the mirror.

Alvarr went out and gathered treasure. He took the hearts of dead Dimensions and the crowns of drowned kings, rivers of authority and seeds of unborn Observable Existences, everything that made his own chest burn with wanting, and he piled it before his Father in a heap that bent the light.
The Father looked at the heap, and then at his son.

"You have brought me everything YOU desire,"he said. "You looked into Existence and saw only your own face in it. This is the mistake of the mirror, and every living thing commits it: to give others what we ourselves want, and call it generosity. Do not be ashamed. Be corrected. To find what another lacks, you must first put down the mirror and listen. Go again."
And so the Descendant went on and commited another mistake!
The third mistake was the mistake of pride.

Alvarr resolved to listen, and so he sought out the oldest and grandest beings in existence, Primeval things and sovereign things and Provenance Lifeforms, and he asked them what a being such as his Father could lack. They gave him grand answers, and every answer was wrong.
At the edge of a small Observable Existence, a farmer who was nothing at all offered him directions, and Alvarr did not stop, because what could nothing at all know?
He wandered another Age. When he finally passed that way again, humbled and worn, he stopped at the same field, and the farmer gave him the same directions, and they were true ones.
When he told his Father, the Father nodded slowly.

"Pride is the worst of the mistakes," he said, "not because it is the largest, but because it is the jailer of all the others. Every mistake can be cured by asking. Pride is the mistake that forbids asking. A being who cannot ask can only repeat. Remember the farmer. Go again."
And he went on!
The fourth mistake was the mistake of the closed hand.

Following the farmer’s directions, Alvarr came upon a wonder: a dying beast of the old dark, and cradled in its fading coils, a thing that existed nowhere else, offered freely to whoever would take it before the beast’s last breath.
And Alvarr hesitated.

Was it a trick? Was it worthy? Was he? He weighed, and he doubted, and he waited to be certain, and while he waited, the beast breathed its last, and the wonder went out with it, and no power in all existence could light it again.
"I made no move at all,"he told his Father, bitter. "How can doing nothing be a mistake?"

"Because hesitation is not the absence of a choice," the Father said. "It is a choice wearing the mask of caution. The closed hand believes it is keeping itself safe. It is only keeping itself empty. Some doors open once, my son. You will grieve this one for a long time, and the grieving is also the learning. Go again."
And this fucker went on to commit yet another mistake.
The fifth mistake...was the mistake of the buried wound.
For in his wanderings Alvarr had erred against a companion, a small betrayal, committed in a weak hour, and rather than confess it, he had hidden it, and told himself it was too small to matter.
But a hidden mistake is a planted one!

It grew in the dark. The small betrayal became a distance, and the distance became a silence, and the silence became a parting, and by the time Alvarr understood what he had buried, the companion was gone beyond finding, carrying a wound with no name on it.
He confessed it to his Father last of all, and his voice failed him twice in the telling.

"Now you know the accounting every liar learns too late,"the Father said. "A mistake confessed is half repaired. A mistake hidden compounds. Shame promises to protect you from the cost of your errors, and instead it collects interest on them. Bury nothing, my son. The buried does not rot. It grows. Go again."
Finally, lastly, he commited his last mistake.
The sixth mistake was the mistake of the ended story.
Alvarr did not go again.

He sat down at the rim of a dead Dimension, and he counted his failures, one Age of haste, one Age of mirrors, pride, an empty hand, a buried wound and its silense, and he concluded that he was a being MADE of mistakes, and that a being made of mistakes could bring his Father nothing, and that the quest was over because he was over.
He sat there for a long time. Long enough that the dust of the dead Dimension began to know him.
And at last, because there was nothing else left to do, he stood up anyway, and walked home to say the failure aloud rather than let it also become a buried thing.
He came before his Father with his hands open and empty.
"I have failed the quest," Alvarr said. "I searched every reach of existence, and I found nothing you lack. I bring you nothing. Only my mistakes."
There was a long silence!
And then the Father did something the record insists upon, though it strains believing. He leaned forward, and his ancient existence trembled, and he said:
"Say that last part again."
"...I bring you only my mistakes."
"Then the quest is complete," the Father said. "You have brought me the one thing I do not have."
BOOM!
Alvarr stared at him, uncomprehending, and the Father spoke on, and the record keeps his words whole:

"I am one of Those Who Remain. When I speak, existence is supposed to agree. I have never reached for a thing and missed it. And so I have never once, in all the reaches of my existence... learned anything. A mistake is a teacher that existence sends for free, and no teacher has ever been permitted to reach me!"

And so it was, the record says, that every evening for an Age, a being whom existence obeyed sat quietly in the dark and was taught by his own child, hungering after the one wealth he could never mint!
The record ends with three sayings.
To err is to be alive. Stones are flawless, and they are stones.
A mistake is only a failure if it is the last one you consult.

And the young make mistakes and become old. The old make mistakes and become wise. The wise make mistakes and become stories, and the stories go on erring in the mouths of everyone who retells them, and this too is how the living remain alive.
But not all of Those Who Remain listened the way this Father listened. Some paint an entirely different picture that would make one question whether Those Who Remain were so grand and wise.
Because some believe Those Who Remain are filled with faults, and no more grander than any other lifeform out there.
That is another story.
<THE True Human Emperor>
It was human to make mistakes.
Noah Osmont was human.
So he made a mistake!

It did not look grand when he made it. Mistakes rarely do. His mistake was only this: he pulled all nine of his clones out of THE Ymnaros and into THE Infiniverse, to stand among his people, to place eighteen hundred beginnings into the right hands, to watch his daughter’s face as she held nine seeds of her own. A father’s errand. A ruler’s errand. A few hours of work inside his own home!
And it did not seem like anything at all!

Damodred was out there. Hvitrmarr was out there, a queen who had broken her own chains. Anaximander was out there, and nothing in existence had ever managed to file him. Skallagrim stood guard at the very door with a Steed at his side and all twenty of Attributes in his frame. Four of the mightiest beings Noah had ever gathered, watching a Dimension at peace, and if anything happened, anything at all, he could be there in a short period of time.
Or so he thought!
It arrived in the span of a nanosecond.
Noah was standing in the golden light of his mother’s realm with Tesseracts turning around him in their slow orbit, and between one beat of his Heart and the next, the threads went dark!

Hvitrmarr’s thread, the Blood Duke’s bond of crimson gold running from his existence to hers, snuffed out between one instant and the next! Damodred’s presence, wrapped in his authority, gone! The weavings he had seated across the key figures of an entire Dimension, dozens of them, extinguished instsntly in a single silent moment, and through the one thread that remained, through Skallagrim’s Sovereign bond, strained taut and screaming, sensations poured into him that made his blood turn cold and then ignite!
Shackled!
Inhibited!
IMPRISONED!

His people! His guardians! Beings he had healed and freed and seated with his own hands, silenced across gigaparsecs in less time than a thought takes to finish, and something in him went very still and very quiet, and then everything in him that was not still and not quiet stood up at once!
Fury rolled off his body as the golden fields bent flat around him!

Sanguine light erupted around his body as from different direction, nine crowns of blood tore themselves away, and his hands were already moving, and in the distance, along the cliff above the radiant river...
Thalia Vasiliou frowned.

She was standing beside his mother with a fishing line still in her hand, and her head had turned upward, toward the skies of THE Infiniverse, toward the outside, exactly toward the place where his threads had died, and her narrowed eyes seemed to reach through his home’s endless blue to the wound beyond it!
And her thought arrived in his mind, low and level and grim.
’This force? This early?’
His racing paused on those words!

’Those are particularly troublesome ones, and their backing is unfathomably deep.It would hurt me a great deal to give you any information about them. So you may have to put in a bit of work with these ones yourself. Try any way you can to obtain information about them, and...’
The pause stretched!
’...I am sorry for any pain of your people they and you are about to have.’
She said such heavy words, and Noah did not answer her, because there was nothing to answer with, and because he was already gone!
He set off!
His clone came to a stop in the crossing-dark outside THE Ymnaros, and stood opposite the leader of those who had attacked his Dimension and his people!

She stood with her back to a half-collared Sovereign wrapped in hundreds of white blades. A plain woman in plain garments, dark hair bound back, pale eyes, no authority anywhere on her at all, and at her feet, chained and pinned and headless, lay the corpse of a small Steed that had been free for less than a single day!
And she looked into the cold rage of his manifestation without a flicker, and told him what she wanted.
Him!
His body, delivered to her hands, in exchange for every chained and caged and inhibited existence his mistake had left behind!
It was human to make mistakes.
Noah was human.
And outside THE Ymnaros, in the crossing-dark, the price of his was standing in front of him with pale, patient eyes, waiting to be paid!

chapters.title: Chapter 5615: The Golden Leash!
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
He looked at Yrsa coldly, and his eyes flashed!
THE Protagonist’s Omniscient Regard swept across the leader of the incursion as it reached for her truths, and her details unfolded before him as the crossing-dark itself seemed to lean in!
|Warden Yrsa|:: VERITAS: 23. PROVENANCE: 0. POTENTIA: 25. PONDUS: 28. A Warden of ???. Her origin is ???. She has never once broken a rule she set for herself. ???
Every attribute, apart from Provenance, above twenty!

Every single one! Above the wall of ten that had once capped his own sight, sitting in the range where Skallagrim’s completed panel sat and climbing past it, all of it seated inside a being who radiated absolutely nothing at all! Her PONDUS alone stood at twenty-eight, a bearing grander than a Blood Sovereign’s, wrapped in plain garments and a clerk’s calm!
Questions stacked themselves in his depths, and Noah set every one of them aside, because his rage had not moved an inch and neither had he!
He was undaunted.
He looked at the panel, and then at her, and when he spoke, his voice rolled out grand and cold across the crossing-dark.

"You have made yourself my enemy just now."His crimson gold eyes held her pale ones. "And because I am so fucking magnanimous, I give you this one chance to change course. In existence, when the many are dying and getting collapsed, they always wish they had done something different in the past. Some moment where the road forked, and they took the wrong side of it."
He let the dark hold the words. "That moment, for you, is this one. Change your course. Release my people... and you may yet have salvation in your future."
Yrsa listened to all of it without a flicker.
And then she smiled, calmly.
"I do not fear death." She said it plainly. "For my cause, I can gladly die. If what I am doing now becomes the reason I die in some future? I have no qualms about it at all."
Her head tilted. "But that is me. You... have these people I have chained."
Her pale eyes did not leave his.

"So, to show you how serious I am. In the next nanosecond, I will start by breaking the bones of the steed you cured and took from THE Krazhor-Nul Dimension.Or you can bring your main body here, alongside a certain Remnant Existential Treasure, and make the exchange. I will even honor you properly."
She waved her hand!
HUUM!
Light bloomed above her palm as a collar band manifested there, and it was not gray!

It was GOLDEN! A dazzling band of deep gold, seamless and unmarked, turning slowly above her hand as off its surface rolled a silent air of suffocation that pressed against the crossing-dark itself, a pressure that did not attack and did not threaten and simply sat there promising an ending to expression itself!
"A special Inhibitor," Yrsa said. "Meant to stifle the terrifying Descendants of Those Who Remain. I have never yet had cause to use one. For you, I will."
Noah looked at this lifeform coldly as, at the sides of his head, his own voice began to speak!

"We need to collapse every fucking shred of existence that she and her forces have." THE Provenance of the Closed Crown spoke low and flat from his left, arms folded, eyes shut. "Just go utterly apeshit, and figure everything else out later."
"That is feasible,"THE Provenance of the Open Hand answered calmly from his right. "And Hvitrmarr and the others may die in the doing of it. For what? A momentary release of anger?"

The cross-legged figure’s light held even and warm. "Thalia said we need to obtain information about these ones. Brute force is not ideal here, and it is not even efficient. But we have other means. Consider what she is actually asking. She wants to chain us... and we cannot be chained. She does not KNOW we cannot be chained. So we play along. We let her close her collar, and she will take us to wherever this force of hers belongs, into the heart of everything she serves... and we can obtain information in abundance while every one of them believes they are guarding a prisoner. We would gain more there than we could ever gain by overcoming her here. And overcoming her here guarantees casualties."

"At what cost?"the Crown said coldly. "Think of what we are. Think of the stature of what we have built and become. How could someone of our standing be WILLINGLY imprisoned? Leashed? Paraded into their cages by our own consent?"
"Are we truly so prideful?" the Hand asked. "So overly arrogant that we cannot play a part? A prisoner’s part, worn for a while, in exchange for the best results our people can be given?"
Noah listened to all the parts of himself, coldly, completely.
And before a nanosecond had passed...
HUUM!
Beside the clone that had first appeared in the crossing-dark, his main body arrived!

Crimson gold and stellar blue, the collar of First Purity at his chest as eleven singularities turned in his depths, THE True Human Emperor himself stepped out of nothing at all, and he looked at Warden Yrsa as he spoke with total calm.
"My freedom... for my people."
It was something surreal!

Even Yrsa seemed surprised! Her pale eyes moved over him up and down, and then she nodded once and came over unhurried as the golden collar in her grasp opened itself and floated across the dark toward his throat, a leash of dazzling gold hanging still in the silence between them.
"Put it on."
Noah gazed at the thing hanging before him, and prompts unfolded across his sight!
|You are observing a Lineage Inhibitor: THE GILDED CLAUSE.|

|The highest grade of Existential Inhibitor in its order’s records. Where common Inhibitors subtract granted authority, THE GILDED CLAUSE suppresses the genetic and existential expression of any and all authority at its root: granted, devoured, inherited, or written. Intents, Sources, Infinities, Pantheons, and frameworks are stifled at the level of expression itself.Even the sentence-lineage of a Descendant of Those Who Remain, the unbroken written line running back to the speaking hand, is silenced clause by clause while the band remains closed.|
|It adapts. Expressions that attempt to rise are read, and counter-written, faster than they form.|
|Its make is ???. Its count in existence is ???.|
Noah read every line of it coldly.

And he knew, with plain certainty, that it would do nothing to him! It was a masterwork raised against every power existence had ever handed anyone, and nothing he carried had been handed to him! Nothing granted. Nothing borrowed. Nothing owed!
So, calmly and efficiently... Noah put the leash on his own neck!
CLICK!
And in the same instant, he made the oppression around himself disappear!

His pressure folded inward and vanished as his presense dimmed, the weight that bent grass and caved stone withdrawing entirely, until THE True Human Emperor stood in the crossing-dark, collared in gold, and gave off the air of... nothing! Nothing at all! A man, in a band, powerless to every sense that would ever check!
"I detest this," THE Closed Crown said flatly at his ear.

"Going through things one does not like,"THE Open Hand replied, serene, "is part of being human. We do it constantly. We wait, we swallow, we wear what the hour demands, and we do it because the results on the far side may be something unfathomably grand."
Its closed eyes did not open, and its voice settled soft over the golden collar. "To be human... is to do a lot of things one does not like."

chapters.title: Chapter 5616: Promises!
paragraphs: The golden leash sat closed around the neck of THE True Human Emperor.
And beside him, his clone trembled.

The crowned manifestation of blood shuddered once in the crossing-dark as its crimson gold light guttered and dimmed, and then it came apart, seemingly starved of everything that had sustained it, scattering into fading motes that dimmed and went out between one breath and the next!
Gone. As though the band at his throat had reached through him and unmade even the works of his blood!
Yrsa watched the motes fade.
Then she floated over to him, unhurried, and took his hand in hers, and with the casual efficiency of a clerk testing a seal... she broke his finger.
CRACK!

The bone snapped sideways under her grip, and blood welled dark at the joint, and the finger stayed broken! No stellar light rushed to it. No mending crawled beneath the skin. Nothing in him rose to answer the injury at all, and Noah allowed every bit of it to happen as he gazed at her coldly, his expression unmoving over a seemingly leashed and powerless body!
Yrsa looked at the broken finger for a moment longer. Then she released his hand, and nodded slowly.

"I am entirely surprised."She drifted back half a step as her pale eyes stayed on his face. "Do you know how many times I have stood before a leader and offered this exact exchange? Their freedom for their people’s. I have offered it to sovereigns of clusters of Observable Existences. To Primeval things with congregations beyond count. To kings whose subjects sang their names in numbers that bent the air."

She shook her head once. "Leaders rarely put themselves on the line for their people. Almost never. They would rather their people die, every last one of them, than give up their rulership. They tell themselves they will avenge the dead after, as if vengeance were a kind of protection they could pay in arrears. I have heard that reasoning so many times I could recite it in my sleep."
Her gaze moved over the golden band at his throat.
"You actuslly stood for your people! For that... I will stick to my word, and release your people."
She raised her fingers and gestured once!

The shrouded beings appeared around them in silence, white-wrapped figures with Loom-rivers turning in orbit, circling Noah in a loose ring with their presense registering nowhere, and one of them drifted forward bearing a set of golden chains that uncoiled in the dark and wound themselves around Noah’s hands, coiling wrist to wrist in dazzling links that clicked softly as they settled!
And Noah did not watch the chains.
He gazed past them, at Skallagrim.

The Blood Sovereign still stood half-bound where she had left him, the wedged band at his throat, and the eyes of this Descendant were RAGING! Crimson gold seas churned in them with a violence that had no outlet, fixed on the leashed figure of the man who had rewritten his lineage, and his shroud of unpaid deaths strained against the band in useless ragged pulses!
Yrsa waved her hand.

The hundreds of Argent Loom swords orbiting him dissolved, blades unraveling back into loomlight and draining away into the dark, and in the next instant she waved her hand again, and the half-closed Inhibitor around Skallagrim’s neck opened instsntly, releasing its grip clause by clause as it floated back across the crossing-dark toward her waiting palm!
HUUM!
Skallagrim erupted!

Power detonated out of the Descendant as his crimson gold seas came roaring back to full flood, all twenty of Attributes in his frame igniting at once, and the surrounding existence MELTED, the crossing-dark itself running and warping around his fury for light years as his fissures blazed and his shroud whipped wide!
And Yrsa smiled at it.
"I could have unshackled you after we left,"she said, mild and even inside the melting dark. "But I did this here, in front of him, to show your master that I keep my promises."

Her head tilted slightly. "Be a good boy. I am still stronger than you, even while you are not inhibited. Your Master will be gone, and you... should take care of his Dimension, and his people. They will need it."

Her pale eyes did not so much as narrow against the heat of him. "And if we notice anything here that draws our attention again... I cannot promise we will not be back, to put this whole Dimension through processing under full inhibition. So."
A small nod, the nod of a keeper closing up for the day. "Do not let your master’s actions be in vain. Okay?"
With such words, Warden Yrsa drifted back to float beside Noah!

And around them, the rest of her order arrived. Axon descended with his halos turning shoulder to heel, and Ohmran’s vast clay-skinned bulk settled into the dark, and the many shrouded lifeforms they had come with gathered in from every direction, dozens of white-wrapped figures with rivers of the Loom in orbit, all of them closing into formation around a single leashed and chained Human Emperor!
Noah stood at the center of all of it, golden at the throat and golden at the wrists, and his cold gaze swept across Skallagrim one last time!
And in the next instant, all of them disappeared!
The crossing-dark emptied. The white rivers closed.

And left behind in all that silence stood Jarl Skallagrim, wreathed in his own useless erupting power... and the chained, headless corpse of a small Steed that had been free for less than a single day.
Moments later, existence split!

Anaximander appeared in the region with his robes still and his eyes cold, and the anger on the scholar’s face was a thing that had never once been seen there in all his wandering, and he looked around the empty crossing-dark, at the melted scars of Skallagrim’s eruption, at the corpse, at the nothing where an entire incursion force had stood!
"Where did they go?"His voice came out low, and then it cracked upward! "WHERE?!"
He asked as...even he could not sense it!
Skallagrim did not answer.
The Blood Sovereign stood with his fists shaking at his sides, filled with a boundless fury that had nowhere at all to go, and he could not even bring himself to speak!
And in THE Ymnaros Dimension, the promises were being kept.
On the northern shelf, high in its stacked cage, a shackle came loose from Hvitrmarr!

The gray band at her throat released, and the chains unwound from her legs and wings and jaws, and her nine transforming organs came roaring back awake inside her as her power flooded home, and THE Blood Duke rose inside the metal box and broke it, tearing the cage apart from within as dull gray plates rained down the sky, and she burst out into the open air with her red gold wings flung wide and ROARED!
HUUM!

The roar rolled across gigaparsecs! It shook the shelf and the fields and the far terraces, a sound of rage and grief and three thousand years of chains pressed into a single note, and it did not sound anything at all in it of freedom!
And above the citadel, Damodred appeared.
The last Laestrygonian stood unshackled in the air over the streets where they had taken him, his blindfold of crimson gold hands alive once more and opened wide around the single great eye beneath!
Below him lay what the taking had cost.

The casualties were still there. Hundreds of Humans lay broken across the stone in blood and death, the trampled and the crushed, small figures being lifted and wept over and carried, a street that had been a market this morning, and the survivors moved through it slowly under the floating cages’ empty shadows!
Damodred looked down at all of it.
And his single eye pulsed with a terrifying rage!

chapters.title: Chapter 5617: THE ETERNAL PAX! I
paragraphs: Purple gold strings surrounded everything.

Noah stood leashed and chained in an area walled by them on every side, countless strings pulsing and thrumming as they moved at tremendous speeds through the dark, each one racing along its own path as though it had a set destination it had crossed a billion times before, and his senses read them quietly from behind an expression of nothing at all!
The Argent Loom. Expressed differently here, dyed purple gold and woven into roads!

Around him, the incursion force stood in loose formation as Warden Yrsa gave her orders, clipped and efficient, and group after group of shrouded ones bowed and stepped onto the racing strings and vanished along them, dozens of departures in moments, until the transit dark held only four figures: Noah, Yrsa, the vast clay-skinned Primeval with a pale band at its own throat... and the being wrapped in turning halos.
And at this time, prompts rose before Noah’s eyes alone!
|You have remained quintessentially true to your Provenance.|

|You were threatened, and you did not bend. You were collared, and you were not contained. You walked into the hands of your enemies as an act of your own design, wearing their chains as instruments of your own aim, and at no point did your existence argue with itself. To be true under freedom is common. To be true under a leash is generation.|
|Your attributes have increased.|
|VERITAS: 15. PROVENANCE: 11. POTENTIA: INFINITE. PONDUS: 17.|
Growth! Here, of all places! Chained at the wrists and collared in gold at the center of an enemy formation, and his existence had weighed all of it and called it truth, and grown!
As he read the panel, Yrsa moved!

Her leg swiped at his feet without warning, and Noah played along perfectly, his stance breaking as he fell back and sat down hard against the dark, chains rattling, and Yrsa lowered herself to sit beside him, entirely at ease, and when he looked at her, her pale eyes were shining with open interest and wonder!

"What an interesting thing you are." She studied his face. "Capable of curing the Cursed Steeds and the Cursed Descendants made so by THE Sleepless Fiend himself. And you ran circles around THE Sealed One to obtain the Remnant Existential Treasure he wanted so badly." Her gaze dropped to his chest."Is that it, by the way?"
She reached out to the Aurate Collar!
And the moment her finger touched the ancient bone...
SSSS!
Her finger singed!

It was a reaction of touching the sun itself! Pale skin scorched black at the tip in an instant as a thread of smoke curled up between them, and Yrsa pulled her hand back with genuine surprise crossing her face for the first time since the crossing-dark, shaking her finger once as the burn slowly closed!
Noah looked at her coldly.
"A treasure such as this is bound to me by my blood." His voice stayed level. "As long as I live, even grasping it will be an issue for you."
Yrsa smiled at that.

"Is that right?"She flexed her singed finger, unbothered, almost pleased. "You are definitely interesting. Your power may even be close to Axon, or even me, if that Descendant was made what he is under you."
Her smile cooled a fraction. "But all that power means nothing if it is inhibited now, hm?"
Noah felt the golden leash sit against his neck, and he kept his voice calm.
"I saw the prisons and the leashes you almost brought out for THE Ymnaros Dimension." His cold eyes held hers. "Are you doing this to others too? What exactly do you want?"
Yrsa smiled coldly, and then she sighed, and for the first time, she truly began to talk.

"Authority." She said the word with an old, cold weight. "In the hands of the unworthy, existence suffers. It has always suffered. It suffers right now, in a hundred thousand places at once, because some random thing climbed a random ladder and was handed a hammer at the top of it, and existence never once checked what would be built."

Her pale eyes did not blink."I am an Enforcer. One among many. Our task is stability, and our method is subtraction: we take away the capability to utilize authority, from the many who should never have held it. Existence’s randomness hands authority to too many, too easily, with no test and no ledger."She turned her head to him.
"We are the answer to that randomness."
Noah listened to all of it, and then he spoke, grand and quiet.

"And who are you to pick and choose who is unworthy of authority?"His chained hands rested still in his lap. "Line up every being you have ever collared, and every judgment you made over them. Who weighed YOU? What gives you the right?"
"Why..." Yrsa’s answer came without a heartbeat of delay, serene and total. "Existence gave us the right, of course. We would not have the right otherwise."
Noah gazed coldly at her.
"Then I can assume one of Those Who Remain paved the way for all this. Or several of them."He let it land. "You should be just the hounds of someone with a true vision."
Yrsa laughed at that, one short breath of it, and she waved her hand as she pointed lazily across the transit dark, at the haloed being, at the collared Primeval!
"Others may be hounds." Her smile spread. "But some of us have that glorious vision ourselves. Haha! And you will see a glimpse of it, as we... are here."
HUUM!
The purple gold strings around them pulsed once, brilliantly, and faded!
|You have crossed an unfathomable distance. You have arrived in an unknown Dimension.|
And existence opened up around Noah.

He stood upon a purple gold floating mountain! Its slopes fell away beneath him in terraces of radiant stone, and it was one among MANY, dozens of serene floating mountains drifting upon endless seas of white clouds, each one glowing softly in gold and violet, arranged in a vast outer ring around deeper reaches where more mountains rose, grander and brighter, ascending toward some far center that burned too radiant to look at directly!
It was beautiful. It was serene past anything an incursion force had any right to come home to!
And then Noah looked outward, past the ring, at what surrounded the mountains.
Cages.
Countless stacked cages extending for light years!

They filled the skies beyond the outer ring in every direction, gray cubical prisons of that same seamless metal stacked upon each other in columns and walls and gigaparsec reaches, tier upon tier upon tier, an architecture of captivity vast enough that his eyes could follow a single column of cages upward until it thinned into the distance and never find its end!
And they were full!

Some cages held clusters, dozens of Source Lifeforms crowded together in one box, their dense patient light guttered to almost nothing, or huddles of Infinite Lifeforms whose silver seas lay still, or crowds of Gilded Ones whose brilliance had gone out entirely, dim golden figures sitting shoulder to shoulder in the dark of their boxes!

Other cages held lone figures, single True Lifeforms in single boxes, beings who had crossed the threshold of Trueness itself sitting alone with their heads down! And other cages, set apart and wound with extra bands of loomlight, held lone PRIMEVAL Lifeforms, ancient things older than frameworks, lying motionless along the floors of metal boxes!
And as Noah gazed across them, what struck him hardest was not the count.
It was the stillness!

So many of the jailed looked despondent past all reaching, without any will left to live at all! Beings sat unmoving with their eyes open and empty. A Source Lifeform leaned against its bars with one hand stretched out through them, reaching toward a cage across the golden road where smaller lights huddled, and the hand simply hung there, unmoving. It had been reaching for a long, long time!
His eyes flashed, and panels unfolded across the nearest of them!
|A True Gilded Lifeform|:: VERITAS: 0.8 (0, Inhibited). PROVENANCE: 0. POTENTIA: 0.6 (0, Inhibited). PONDUS: 0.7 (0, Inhibited). She has stopped counting the days.
|A True Infinite Lifeform|:: VERITAS: .4 (0, Inhibited). PROVENANCE: 0. POTENTIA: 1.9 (0, Inhibited). PONDUS: 1.1 (0, Inhibited). He no longer remembers the sound of his own Pantheon.

Beside every true value, in the parenthesis, flat and total: (0, Inhibited). What they were, and what they were now permitted to express!
And then he saw the roads.
Down the wide golden roads that ran between the cage-walls, shrouded beings were leading rows of inhibited lifeforms!

Lines of them, hundreds long, collared and chained wrist to wrist, shuffling between the stacked prisons toward open cages waiting with their doors ground wide, and the lines moved in silence, and the silence was the silence of beings who had already learned!
Because as Noah watched, one did not move in silence!
A Gilded Lifeform midway down a row stopped walking! It turned at an open cage door and refused, planting itself, shaking its dimmed head, and its mouth opened.
"I am SUPERBIUS! Do you understand this? My pride burns even now-...!"

Two shrouded ones descended on it instsntly, and they beat it! They beat it down onto the golden road with blows that cracked across the distance, methodical and unhurried, and the row around it stood still and stared at their own feet, and when the Gilded Lifeform still dragged itself up one more time and reached for the shroud of the nearest one...
It was killed.

One blow, dispensed with the same clerical efficiency as all the rest, and a being that had once been brilliance itself splattered across the golden road, its dimmed light bursting apart and raining down over the stone and over the feet of its own row, and the shrouded ones stepped over what remained and gestured the line forward, and the line moved!
The golden road drank the light, and did not change color!
Noah looked at all of it. The mountains. The cages. The reaching hand. The road.
And he turned to Yrsa, and his voice came out heavy.
"Is this... your vision?"His chained hands did not move. "Lifeforms in cages? This brutality, occurring all around?"
Yrsa harrumphed!
She looked around at the whole of it, the columns and the roads and the stillness.

"I do not like this any more than you."She said it plainly. "But things must be done for prosperity. All are chained for NOW, because we are in the process of collecting. Do you understand? This is the middle of the work, not the end of it. Domains and Observable Existences are being prepared and cleared out at this very moment, and we have already begun transporting the collected to them, where, with no authority at all, they will learn to build their own Civilizations again. As normal lifeforms."

Her voice steadied into the cadence of a thing recited and believed. "Farmers. Workers. Soldiers. Protectors. All of it without a shred of authority anywhere among them, and no hammer for existence to hand to anyone ever again. We usher in an era of peace."

Her pale eyes moved to the stain on the golden road below. "Those who rebel against this vision, even after they are told not to be unruly... those are the only ones that can make things here seem brutal. But we..."
She looked back at him.
"We are good. We are good."
HUUM!
She rose, and moved behind Noah, and kicked him forward!

He stumbled ahead as a white cloud of Argent Loom formed beneath their feet, catching them both, and it began to float across the mountain’s radiant terraces as the wind of the heights moved over them, and Noah focused his senses outward as they flew!
And he felt them!

Terrifying auras, many of them, seated across the deeper mountains! A presense of weight after weight that he had rarely felt anywhere in existence, each one settled on its own peak within the inner rings, patient and immense!

Yrsa smiled.

"Welcome... to THE Serenaros!"Her arms spread wider. "One of the seats of stability across existence! The answer to every unworthy hand! Welcome, O Blood-Crowned One..."
Her pale eyes shone down at him.
"...to THE ETERNAL PAX!"
"The Pax provides, The Pax protects, The Pax subtracts! The Pax is here for the glory and stability of Existence!"

Expressed differently here, dyed purple gold and woven into roads!

SSSS!
Her finger singed!
It was a reaction of touching the sun itself!

What gives you the right?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5618: THE ETERNAL PAX! II
paragraphs: THE ETERNAL PAX.

Of course, a name told you what a thing wished to be, not what it was. Noah turned the ridiculous title over as the cloud carried them on, and behind him Yrsa yawned and stretched, in the manner of a woman who felt she had done quite enough for one cycle.
The distant figures she had been commanding fell away behind them, and then it was only the two of them, crossing the vibrant mountains alone.
Since the crossing was long, Noah was able to see many things.

The first was the strangeness of the shrouded figures. In the areas they passed, many of them moved about continuously, leading rows and hauling chains along the golden roads, and that much was ordinary enough.
But others were not moving at all.

They stood straight and stationary in ordered clusters across the terraces, dozens together, unbreathing and unswaying, and the longer he looked at them, the more a question settled in him. Were these truly lifeforms at all? Or was he looking at an army of things that only wore the shape of one?
His eyes flashed quietly, and details bloomed.
|You are observing THE LOOMWROUGHT SHROUDS.|

|Artificial lifeforms of THE ETERNAL PAX, born from woven authority and unknown technology. Each is grown around a core of refined Argent Loom and wrapped in a body manufactured to a single exacting standard. They do not eat, do not rest, do not age, and do not question any orders. They activate upon assignment and stand down upon completion.|
|A Loomwrought Shroud|:: VERITAS: 11. PROVENANCE: 0. POTENTIA: 11. PONDUS: 11. It has never asked a question.

He swept his gaze across the stationary clusters, panel after panel unfolding, and every one of them read exactly the same. Eleven, eleven, eleven, across every attribute, on every figure, without a single decimal of deviation. Compared to the wild variance he had seen in the caged, where a Primeval measured differently in every limb of its panel, this uniformity said something all its own.
A grown thing varied. A made thing matched. And someone, somewhere, had made a very great number of soldiers who each carried the weight of a weak Primeval Lifeform!
How many of them existed? How long had they been standing?
Ahead of him, Yrsa laughed.

"Why look around so much?" She did not even turn. "It is not like anything you see here will help you. Once jailed, there is not really any going back. Many powerful beings realized this in time. You are in it for the long haul, as your fate will be decided soon enough."
Noah said nothing to that, and continued observing coldly. After all, she believed the leash at his neck was working.
At the sides of his head, his own voices spoke instead.
"We could begin by nuking this entire place,"THE Closed Crown said. "The mountains, the roads, the towers. Make sure nothing here leaves alive, and let existence sort out what it lost."
"Destruction can come in time," THE Open Hand answered. "Right now, we understand. We already paid the price of being chained, and the price is spent. So we collect as much as possible against it."
In truth, there was a great deal to collect.

He saw processing terraces cut into the mountainsides, where inhibited lifeforms stood sorted into queues by their varieties, Source with Source and Gilded with Gilded, each line advancing toward seated figures in layered robes. Every collar was touched in turn, and floating ledgers of purple gold script recorded each one’s informstion into some greater count.

Farther out, cage-caravans slid along the string-roads between mountains, boxes in trains a thousand long, bound for reaches he could not see the end of. In the middle distance, silent crews of Shrouds were hollowing out an entire mountain, carving its radiant stone into tier upon tier of empty archive.
Compared to what he had first assumed, an incursion force with a fortress behind it, this was something else entirely. This was a complex organization!

Ultimately, they came to one of the larger mountains, and Yrsa guided the cloud down toward a single purple tower on its upper slopes. The tower was tall, windowless, and smooth, and they passed through its gates on foot, his chains ringing softly in the quiet.

The halls inside were filled with Loomwrought Shrouds. They lined the corridors in stationary rows, filling alcoves and junctions, and some of them had clearly stood in their places for centuries. Not one turned its head as a leashed emperor walked past.

At a wide junction, another figure came out of a side hall. An Enforcer, judging by the layered robes and the purple gold sash, broad and scarred, with a ledger of light folded under one arm. He stopped when he caught sight of them, and looked Noah up and down with open appraisal.
"Warden Yrsa." A nod."I heard you bagged a unique one?"
"Mind your own business, Enforcer Halvard."said Warden Yrsa, and kept walking.
The Enforcer laughed once behind them before his expression became cold as he moved on. Noah noted the exchange without comment.
The corridor ended at massive purple gold doors, and they ground open before Yrsa’s raised hand.
What lay past them was, of all things, a mess.

The great hall beyond was cluttered from wall to wall. Loomwrought Shrouds filled it, though not in ordered ranks. Some stood active, drifting between tables on silent errands, while others slumped against the walls and across benches as if they simply were not operational, white-wrapped bodies folded over in the manner of set-down tools.

Hundreds of collars and leashes lay strewn about in heaps and coils, gray bands and golden bands, whole and half-made and taken apart, spread across tables and hanging from racks and pooling on the floor between instruments Noah had no names for.

Yrsa entered with shining eyes, looking straight ahead, and Noah understood why quickly enough. At the center of the clutter sat an area where even he was forced to focus, because a boundless immensity rested there without bothering to announce itself!
A figure stood at a long table with his back to them.

He was tall and lean. Pale gold hair fell straight and unbound down his back, and every thread on him was royal: a long coat of deep black, high-collared, worked with fine gold embroidery down its seams, over a white shirt whose laced collar rose elegant at his throat, a dark half-cloak hanging from one shoulder.
Upon his brow, half-veiled by the pale hair, sat a small mark of pure obsidian.Amid all the mess of his own making, he alone was immaculate!
This was Descendant Mahishasura!
