chapters.title: Chapter 5625: Cure-Giver!
paragraphs: As his existence advanced and began to expand his rulership across Lifeforms...his body in one of the domains in THE ETERNAL PAX continued its role of a Prisoner.
There was a door in the back of Mahishasura’s workshop that did not look like it went anywhere important.
Yrsa walked him through it on his golden leash, Mahishasura leading with a host’s unhurried pleasure, and between one step and the next, the workshop was gone.
Sunlight fell from no sun.

White marble colonnades. Terraced gardens. Olive trees older than some frameworks, shallow pools mirroring a ceiling pretending to be sky, couches of carved marble circling long low tables, the smell of crushed herbs and old wine!
Compared to the cage-fields outside, it was a paradise. Compared to anything honest, a display case.
And lounging through the whole of it were Cursed Descendants.
’Seven,’Noah counted behind his cold expression. ’And not one curse is the same....’

At the longest table, a mountain of a being ate. The table held enough to feed a citadel. He worked through it with both hands, steady, joyless, and the food replenished itself, and so did his emptiness!
By the largest pool, a slender Descendant lay with a wine bowl on her stomach and her eyes shut, two silent Shrouds refilling it, and her stillness had nothing of rest in it.
Near the entrance, a lean flushed figure declaimed poetry to three Shrouds that had not been built to applaud, his voice pitching louder whenever a living gaze drifted off him.
And at the farthest couch, apart from everything, one Descendant sat upright with his hands folded, watching the door they had just come through.
"Brethren." Mahishasura’s soft voice carried without being raised. Every head turned. The eater paused with his hands full.
"You have waited a long time, and you have heard me make a great many promises. Today, I have outdone them all as...The Pax Provides."
HUUM!
He stepped aside. He gestured to the leashed man, and made the gesture a small ceremony.
"I have brought you... your cure."
Silence.
Then the wine bowl slid from the slender one’s stomach and rang against the marble, and she was sitting up, and the hall broke open with voices!
The mountain at the long table looked the leashed man up and down slowly, and did not stop chewing.
"...Are we supposed to eat him?"
"Baelgrim."
"It is an honest question. You say cure, and you point at a creature." He swallowed, and his voice came down flat and hard. "That is a man on a leash, Mahishasura. The fuck is this?"
"I have brought you the being who unbound a recent Curse from our distant cousins in THE Krazhor-Nul Dimension."
The dice stopped rattling.
The poet’s mouth hung open mid-verse. The slender one rose from her couch entirely, and when she spoke, her voice had gone quiet and careful!
"We heard only weavings of rumors of that. Nothing more."
"Weavings of rumor are how such truths travel across Existence, across the thoughts of our Fathers."

Mahishasura drifted toward the couches, one hand trailing the marble."I confirmed it through memories Yrsa here obtained herself. A Cursed Descendant of THE Krazhor-Nul walks free of his sentence, alongside a rather unfortunate dead Steed that died for those memories to be obtained."
Yrsa’s expression did not move.
His eyes quietly flashed, and the room unfolded into panels.
|Descendant Baelgrim|:: VERITAS: 24. PROVENANCE: 0. POTENTIA: 23. PONDUS: 26. Cursed by the ire of Those Who Remain: THE CURSE OF THE BOTTOMLESS TABLE. He has not felt full in eleven thousand years.

|Descendant Sylvaine|:: VERITAS: 27. PROVENANCE: 0. POTENTIA: 25. PONDUS: 24. Cursed by the ire of Those Who Remain: THE CURSE OF THE SHARED WOUND. Every harm she authors arrives in her own flesh first.

|Descendant Othrys|:: VERITAS: 21. PROVENANCE: 0. POTENTIA: 22. PONDUS: 20.Cursed by the ire of Those Who Remain: THE CURSE OF THE UNREMEMBERED NAME. Whoever looks away from him forgets him. His deeds remain; his name does not.

|Descendant Kharvel|:: VERITAS: 29. PROVENANCE: 0. POTENTIA: 27. PONDUS: 28. Cursed by the ire of Those Who Remain: THE CURSE OF THE UNSLEEPING WATCH. He has been made to require sleep and has not slept since the sentence was spoken. He sees more than he wishes to.
Each one was uniquely cursed as the curses themselves tremendously interested Noah!
"Then why is the supposed thing capable of stripping away curses leashed?" Othrys had crossed half the hall already, hungry-eyed, planting himself where the most gazes would have to pass through him.
"If it can do what you say, it is worth more than...many, many things. Why is a thing like that wearing a collar? Or is thst precisely the reason why?"
"Because before he is the cure, he is the Pax’s prisoner."
Hungry gazes all honed in on Noah from many sides!
And then, from the far couch, without rising, a voice worn smooth by many sleepless nights.
"What does it cost?"
The hall quieted. Sylvaine glanced back at the watcher, then at Noah.
"Everyone who gives something wants something,"Kharvel continued, patient, terrible, calm.
"Cure-Giver....What does your cure cost?"
Every gaze in the pocket Dimension settled on the leashed man.
And at both sides of Noah’s head, his own voices echoed out in his mind!

"Look at their power and standing," THE Closed Crown said, low and appreciative. "We can cure their curses while applying our marks on them, being sure to entrench our Provenance Essence so deeply into their existences and code that they don’t even sense it. They will purposefully not get a high tier as at our choosing...we will command them to begin going against this domain and The Pax overall. Descendants...at our beck and call."
HUUM!
"Brother," THE Open Hand said, with something close to warmth, "there are times I like you. This is a sound plan."
HUUM!
Both sides of him agreed!
So he lifted his gaze, chains ringing softly, and answered the only question that had been put to him.
"Healing a Curse of Those Who Remain is unfathomably difficult work. What sits in each of you is not an illness. It is authored weaving of existence, braided through every clause of what you are."
His cold eyes traveled the couches, the pools, the mountain of food, the unsleeping watcher.

"I will need access to the entirety of your existence while I do it. All of it. One of you at a time. And if I face any rejection from you while I am altering the weavings of your existence and releasing the curse... your existence itself could collapse."
He let that settle across the marble.
"And in doing all of this is my freedom. Yes?"His gaze moved, slow and level, to Mahishasura. "Which means I will also need this collar to be removed so I can access my authority."
The pocket Dimension went very quiet, and every Cursed gaze in it swung from the leashed man to their host, and their host’s composed face gave back nothing at all.
Silence held for one heartbeat longer.
Then Baelgrim laughed, huge and hollow, and shoved his endless table back with a scrape that rang down the colonnades.
He rose to his full mountain height. "I will go first, Cure-Giver!"

chapters.title: Chapter 5626: Curing and Shackling!
paragraphs: Of course, the collar came off!
It was never truly a question, however long the silence had stretched after his demand.

Mahishasura had spent his credibility assembling this room, and made promises to every ruined lounger in it. What was a question, and an interesting one, was how frightened they would allow themselves to look while paying it.
"Remove it,"Mahishasura said.
"...." Yrsa’s eyes looked at Noah as if in a warning as she did not yet nove.
"On my authority, and on my head, my dear Yrsa." The soft voice did not rise. "Remove it."
She crossed to Noah without another word, and her pale eyes held his for one long moment, and then she reached out.
CRACK!
THE GILDED CLAUSE opened and slid from his neck, and the golden chains uncoiled from his wrists, and every being of power in the pocket Dimension pulsed at once!

Mahishasura’s immensity rose behind his composed face. Yrsa’s twenty-eight PONDUS leaned forward against the air. Along the colonnades, Loomwrought Shrouds turned their wrapped heads in perfect unison, and even the Cursed on their couches gathered themselves, seven ruined powers coiling, a whole hall of drawn bows aimed at one unbound man!
And the unbound man released... a silent pressure.

Nothing so crude as power. He simply stopped pretending to be nothing, and let a measured portion of something settle outward through the marble and the pools and the olive trees, presence without shape, weight without direction, and the drawn bows found there was nothing to loose at.
He watched them all hold their eruption and then he raised one hand and beckoned, calm as a man calling for tea.
"Come."
WAA!
The mountain came.

He crossed the hall slowly, and sat where Noah pointed, and up close his curse was audible, a low ceaseless complaint from within him, eleven thousand years of a body demanding what it would never receive!
Noah’s wordlessly raised his hand as he didn’t care for small talk, he would find out everything he wanted soon enough!
Crimson gold rose from his palms and drew itself into blades, thin and precise and humming, and he set them to the Descendant’s existence and opened it, and the pocket Dimension held its breath.
What lay inside was a sentence.
One unbroken line of unreadable script, running backward through every ancestor to a hand that had spoken it before frameworks had names, and braided through it, black through gold, with a curse.
THE CURSE OF THE BOTTOMLESS TABLE!
Noah read it once, coldly.
Then he began to unwrite.

The blades moved. The curse fought, the manner in which all authored things fight their unwriting, clauses screaming as they came apart, and Baelgrim’s mountain body shook, and his hands crushed the marble bench beneath him to powder!
HUUM!
Noah was not at all gentle as the process took some time, the minutes rolling by a Descendant tried not to curse!
Clause by clause. Thread by thread. And beneath the visible working, in the same breath, in the same motion, invisible to every eye and every instrument in the pocket Dimension, his other work ran!
As each cleaned clause resealed, something else settled into the seal, written in the same unreadable script the lineage itself was made of.
|The counter-writing of THE CURSE OF THE BOTTOMLESS TABLE has been unwritten at the root.|
|The lineage of Descendant Baelgrim has been resealed. Within the seal, THE PROVENANCE BLOOD MARK has been written as grammar of the line itself. Designation: VEILED.|
|Nothing in existence perceives the Veiled Mark. It is not an addition to be found. It is the language the sentence is now written in.|

|Descendant Baelgrim: a VEILED BLOOD MONARCH. All bindings, boons, and options are withheld from expression until you call upon them.Available to you, at your choosing, forever: his senses. His memories. The option of command. The option of an ending.|
The blades withdrew. The opened existence closed!
And Baelgrim sat very still on the powdered remains of the bench, and his face went strange, and stranger, and his hands rose slowly to his own stomach.
"Baelgrim?"Sylvaine, half-risen across the hall.
"It is... quiet." The mountain’s whisper cracked. "My stomach... it is quiet."
His breath started coming ragged."All these years, and it is... it is QUIET in here!"
He stood, and swayed, and looked at the endless table still heaped with food, and turned his back on it as he felt nothing!
Then Descendant Baelgrim, the Bottomless, put his face in his hands and laughed.
Mahishasura was already moving.
He circled the cured Descendant slowly, and his amber eyes had gone bright and sharp, and his long fingers traced the air around Baelgrim’s body, reading, testing, hunting.
This fucker was confirming that everything was normal and there was nothing they couldn’t see!
"The Curse unwritten...haha, that is nuts!"the Enforcer murmured.
He looked up at Noah, and smiled, and the smile held delight and something else. "You do clean work, Cure-Giver."
"I said what I take, I take from the curse." Noah’s voice stayed flat. "Who is next?"
The next hours remade the room.

Sylvaine came to him with her eyes set, and left the working an hour later shaking, and stood in the middle of the hall, and drew the blade she had not truly used in an Age, and cut the air, and waited, braced, for the echo of harm that had answered every violence of her long life.
Nothing arrived!
She cut again. Again. Faster, wilder, a storm of edges in the marble hall, and nothing arrived, and she stopped with her chest heaving and tears running silently down her face!

Othrys could not sit still for his. He talked through the opening, talked through the pain, talked until the unwriting reached the clause that had eaten his name, and then he went silent for the first time since Noah had entered this Dimension.
When it was done, he stood, and looked around the hall at his gathered brethren, and asked...
"...Look away from me. All of you. Look away, and then look back."
They did.
"Othrys," Baelgrim said.
"Say it again."
"Othrys," said Sylvaine!
And the Descendant of the Unremembered Name sat down on the marble floor right where he stood and wept into his hands while his own name went on being said around him!

The three loungers from the deep couches came one after another, an hour apiece: a Descendant whose shadow had been cursed to strangle what she loved, a Descendant cursed to age one Age for every lie he spoke, a Descendant whose curse Noah did not name aloud, and unwrote just the same.
Each opened. Each unwritten. Each resealed, cured, and Veiled to the root of what they were, rising incredulous and radiant into a hall that grew louder and warmer with every rising.
|Descendant Sylvaine: a VEILED BLOOD MONARCH.|
|Descendant Othrys: a VEILED BLOOD DUKE.|
|Three lineages resealed. Three VEILED BLOOD MONARCHS.|

|THE Tide That Owes Nothing notes what is being given. Grand salvations, granted to beings of the Transfinite Dimensionality. What pools within the Tide has moved past its prior precedent, and continues to grow. It has not yet been asked for.|
And then only one remained.

Kharvel crossed the hall unhurried, upright, and awake. He sat where the others had sat, and folded his hands, and his unsleeping eyes held Noah’s from an arm’s length away, and for a long moment he said nothing at all.
"One question, Cure-Giver." His worn voice came level. "Before you open me. If I see something inside your cure that I was not meant to see and you wish to quiet me... what happens to me?"
The hall’s warmth thinned. Across the marble, Mahishasura’s amber gaze sharpened, and Yrsa’s pale one, and the cured Descendants went quiet.
"There will not be anything not meant to be or see," Noah said.
"I have not slept in many years. I see everything. It is the one thing I do."
Noah remained quiet and didn’t reply!
The unsleeping eyes searched him for one moment longer.
"...Begin."

The blades rose. The existence opened. And this working ran longest of all, and Noah unwrote all of it, clause by clause by clause, while the hall stood silent and the grammar settled invisibly into every seal.
|The counter-writing of THE CURSE OF THE UNSLEEPING WATCH has been unwritten at the root.|
|Descendant Kharvel: a VEILED BLOOD SOVEREIGN. The Veil holds. Nothing perceives it.|
The blades withdrew. Kharvel sat still.

Then his shoulders came down from a height they had held for eleven millennia, and his unsleeping eyes blinked once, slowly, and blinked again, and a look of pure animal disbelief crossed the most watchful face in the pocket Dimension.
"...Heavy," he whispered. "My eyes are... heavy."
WAA!

He did not make it to a couch. Descendant Kharvel, twenty-nine of VERITAS, the watcher of watchers, lay down on the marble floor of the hall right where he was, and closed his eyes, and slept for the first time in many years, and the sound that came out of him was a snore!
HUUM!

The hall broke into celebration around the sleeping body. Wine and roaring laughter and Othrys’s name still being said, Baelgrim’s empty quiet stomach toasted by the whole roaring hall, Mahishasura moving among his collected brethren accepting their gratitude with elegant modesty, every promise he had ever made them kept in a single day!
And at the edge of it all stood the Cure-Giver, unbound and uncollared, watching the celebration with eyes that had gone entirely cold.
’Seven Descendants. Dance! Laugh! Rejoice! You are can be puppets or be killed...at any moment!’
Apart from being able to collapse their Existence and control it, he could also peruse their memories!
Of course, he did not need their permission, and he did not need their waking, and no instrument in THE Serenaros would register so much as a whisper of what came next!
Somewhere beneath the laughter, along seven threads written into the language of seven existences, the option he had built for himself opened quietly for the first time.
Noah gazed at his cured, celebrating, unknowing Veiled.
’Show me...your memories.’
And he began to read!

chapters.title: Chapter 5627: The Unfinished Command!
paragraphs: Seven libraries of memories opened at once.

Of course, from the outside, nothing at all was happening. The hall roared on around the sleeping body of Kharvel, wine moving, Othrys’s name still being said for the joy of saying it, and at the edge of the celebration stood the Cure-Giver with cold eyes and a stillness that read as weariness to anyone who bothered to look.
Inside that stillness, along seven threads written into the grammar of seven existences, Noah read.
And the first thing he learned was that memory has architecture, and one Descendant in particular had the clearest memory!
The others gave him texture. Kharvel gave him everything.
The structure of THE ETERNAL PAX assembled itself across his depths, memory by memory.

At the bottom, the Loomwrought Shrouds. Made, not born, grown in batch-halls around cores of refined Argent Loom, the labor and the soldiery and the furniture of the whole institution, and no one above them thought of them at all!

Above The Shrouds, The Wardens. And here the memories grew thick with ambition, because Wardenship was a career. Wardens earned their standing in counts: collars logged, collections completed, incursions closed without loss, every capture entered into ledgers that followed a Warden!
Wardens competed. Wardens were sponsored, patron Enforcers lifting promising collectors out of the field, and a Warden whose records ran long and clean enough might one day be raised to a mountain.
Because Enforcers like Descendant Mahishasura held mountains!
Each Enforcer of THE Serenaros kept a peak of the inner rings as seat and fief, with Wardens sworn beneath them and Shroud soldiers of their own!
Above the Enforcers sat an Arbiter, one to a Dimension, governor of the whole of it, and the memories of the Arbiter of THE Serenaros all shared one strange quality.
They dimmed near the center.
Every memory that approached the blinding heart of the inner rings lost its edges, detail sliding away the closer any Descendant had ever walked toward that radiance.
’Even their memories avert. Interesting.’
And above The Arbiters, spoken of always in lowered voices, sat THE Still Conclave.
Nine seats. The summit of the whole Pax, its members almost never seen. Nine beings who answered to nothing beneath them and to only one thing above.
The Voice.
Kharvel had not been there at the founding. But Kharvel had watched a Descendant who had.
And the memory of the founding was a grand one!

A gathering of beings of terrifying depth assembled on a bare plain of purple gold, Descendants among them, Primeval things among them, and every one of them standing the way children stand when summoned. No figure appeared. No shape descended.
There was only the Voice.
It arrived without direction, from everywhere and from inside, and it was not loud and it did not need to be, and the memory itself still shook at its arrival!
"Too many unworthy things are playing with authority."
Noah shuddered!
His actual body, standing in a marble hall gigaparsecs from any memory, shuddered, once, from the sheer registered weight of a voice heard thirdhand!
"Reduce the count across existence, meaningfully."
’Who...’ Even his thought came unsteady. ’Which one of them is this?!’
But the memory did not know!

The Descendant who stood on that plain had never learned it. None of them had. The gathered terrors of that day had gone to their long lives and their eventual sentences without ever knowing which of Those Who Remain had spoken!
"And only stop when you are told to."
The Voice ended. The memory ended.
And Noah stood in the celebration hall with cold sweat at his temples and rage arriving right behind it, rage at the fear itself!
He had shuddered from a voice of Those Who Remain!
He shuddered like a Finite thing in a storm as he was enraged!

’How dare I feel fear from merely hearing the voice of such a being? They are not beyond existence. They are lifeforms! Grander Dimensionality, grander depth, and nothing more than that. Nothing more!’
HUUM!
And beneath the rage, he replayed the last message of whatever one of Those Who Remain had uttered
Only stop when you are told to.
He searched Kharvel’s archive for it as...
No stop order had ever come.

The whole towering machine of THE ETERNAL PAX, The Wardens and their records, The Enforcers and their mountains, the Arbiters and the Conclave and the cages running gigaparsecs in every direction, all of it was still executing the last sentence of a command spoken by one of Those Who Remain!
An unfinished command. An engine with no braking instruction, collecting existence piece by piece, waiting with perfect institutional patience for a word that no memory suggested was ever coming.
He internally shook his head as he continued.
The memories of their Lineages came next, because the cured seven carried three of them in their blood.
Descendants, the memories confirmed, did not descend from Those Who Remain generally.
Each line ran back to one architect, one specific being of that grander Dimensionality whose spoken sentence had become a bloodline, and the lines differed the way their architects differed.
Messages into the existence from Those Who Remain were rare for all of them, a fortune or a catastrophe once in a lifetime if it came at all. But the shape of the silence differed.
THE Sleepless Fiend, whose line Baelgrim and two of the couch-loungers carried, spoke seldom and transactionally, bounties and bargains, an architect who treated its own blood as a workforce.

THE Unblinking Shepherd, whose line ran through Kharvel and Othrys, never spoke at all. Its Descendants lived their whole spans inside the feeling of being watched, a pressure of attention with no message in it ever.

And THE Weeping Architect, whose line Sylvaine and the shadow-cursed one carried, sent no words either. Its messages arrived as griefs. A sorrow with no source, settling into a Descendant’s existence for a year or a century.
Three architects!
Noah held the pattern up against everything else he carried.
This was basically a workforce of Those Who Remain!
And then, in a certain memory, he found the exception.
The memory belonged to the liar-cursed Descendant as it told a grand story.
Wardens and Shrouds by the thousand, Inhibitors in racks, the single greatest collection operation the archive held. Target: the great Infinite Lifeforms of a far reach.
Among the targets: THE Infinity Eater.
And....the operation failed.
The only recorded failure of THE ETERNAL PAX!
And after it, the order had come down through THE Still Conclave, and the order was the true treasure:
Cease all operations against THE Infinity Eater. Cease all operations against the Infinite Lifeforms in specified areas!
Noah’s eyes shone brightly as he understood why!

Collaring Infinite Lifeforms stifled their draw of Infinity. And their draw of Infinity was the Eater’s harvest. Every great Infinite Lifeform the Pax subtracted was income subtracted from a fellow Descendant of Those Who Remain, and so the word had come down from somewhere above the Conclave, and the word was stop!
And right now...
Noah was drinking from the Eater’s protected watershed at this very hour, thread by imperceivable thread.
’What does the farmer do when he notices a second hand on his crop?’
One more thing surfaced before he closed the seven libraries, small and sharp, from the gossip that every institution carries.
Warden Yrsa.
The memories of the cured held her at ceremonies but always slightly apart, always slightly deferred as she was a...
Progeny of a Descendant and a Primeval One. And the Primeval One sat on THE Still Conclave.
One of the nine.
’Well.’ Noah watched the plain woman across the hall, the woman who had broken his finger to check a seal, whose death he had decided on a battlefield gigaparsecs ago.
It didn’t fucking change a thing. She would still die!
Around him, the hall roared on as he...began seeing budding outline of a plan!

chapters.title: Chapter 5628: Accountable!
paragraphs: The celebration was winding down when Warden Yrsa appeared behind him with the golden collar open in her hands.
"Your service has concluded, big guy"she said. "Protocol resumes."

Noah lowered his head slightly, and let her close THE GILDED CLAUSE around his neck, and the click of it rang through a hall that had gone quiet and uncomfortable at the sight, seven cured Descendants watching their miracle be leashed again.
"None of that," Mahishasura had said hours ago, about a shove.
He said nothing at all about a collar.
And within Noah, behind the lowered eyes of a compliant prisoner, his two halves were in session!
"We have everything," THE Open Hand said. "All the memories. The plan was information, and the plan is complete."

"The plan has matured," THE Closed Crown answered. "Look at the room, brother. Every asset of this workshop is standing in one sealable box. An Enforcer whose measure we now hold. A Warden whose blood ties to the ninth chair. Seven Veiled Descendants that answer to our commands. This opportunity will not reassemble itself easily"

"Kharvel watched Mahishasura for two thousand years without blinking." The Crown’s voice echoed. "The seven compared themselves to him constantly. Their reckoning agrees: deep, but not past the middle thirties in attributes. Four of them hold him for a breath. Seven hold him for longer. Seven, plus surprise, plus a sealed Dimension, plus us... hold him for as long as we need."
"And Yrsa?"
"Yrsa," said the Crown, "is mine."
A pause, and then the Hand, quietly: "Seal the box."
HUUM!
It began with nothing anyone could see.

Along seven threads written into the language of seven existences, options opened. Not commands, not yet, only readiness, and seven celebrating Descendants felt nothing at all as their bodies became pieces on a board they could not perceive!

Through the Weft-thread bound quietly to this pocket Dimension a while ago, crimson rivers only one being could see slid across every seam and door and fold of the marble abode, and latched, and held.
The box sealed. No signal would leave it. Nothing would leave it!
Then, gently, a thread pulled.
Baelgrim, laughing, waved Mahishasura over toward the long table. "My friend! Come, sit with us. For years I could not taste food, only need it. Sit, and watch a man eat for joy."
And Mahishasura came, of course, smiling his composed smile, drifting into the heart of his collection’s happiness, accepting wine he did not drink, seating himself among cured brethren!
Sylvaine drifted to his left, telling him of the blade. Othrys took his right, making him say the name again. The three loungers closed in behind with their cups, warm, adoring, casual.
And across the hall, on the marble floor, Kharvel’s eyes opened from the first sleep of many millennia, clear and rested and calm, and he rose without a sound.
Yrsa noticed none of it. Why would she? A host among his grateful cured, a hall full of joy, a prisoner standing collared and docile at her side.
Seven Descendants moved in the same instant, in complete silence.
No shout. No flare!

Baelgrim’s arms closed around Mahishasura’s body from the side with the whole of a mountain’s mass behind them, Sylvaine’s blade was through his shoulder before the wine in his hand had finished falling, Othrys and the three took his limbs, and Kharvel arrived last and struck once, precisely, at a point below the Enforcer’s ribs where its lineage was written heavily, and the composed immensity of Descendant Mahishasura hit his own marble floor under the mass of his entire collection!
BOOOOM!
The pocket Dimension shook!
"Wh-" Yrsa’s wravings of protocol shattered!
Her pale eyes went wide, flicking from the pile of silent violence to the exits that were no longer exits, shock and horror arriving on a face that had never once worn either. "What... what is-"
And beside her, the collared prisoner rose from his docile stillness, unhurried, and rolled his neck against the golden band.
"Crazy stuff, isn’t it?"Noah said mildly. "Existence is truly vast, and full of terrors."
Yrsa turned to him very slowly, and the shock on her face cooled and hardened into something ancient.
"This is your doing?!"
Noah did not reply.

Instead, at the sides of his head, two small figures of stellar blue-gold stirred, and one of them, the cross-legged one, bowed out, and the other, arms folded, dark gold at its edges, opened its eyes for the first time.
"My turn,"said THE Closed Crown.
And it stopped being a figure at his temple, and became him.
HUUM!

The transformation rolled through Noah’s body from the marrow outward. His stature rose, broadened, settled heavier, shoulders widening beneath a mantle of pressure that bent the marble floor into a shallow bowl beneath his feet!

Dark gold bled into the crimson of his aura and hardened at its edges. His hair lifted and darkened at the roots, his features cut themselves a fraction crueler, and his eyes went deep burning gold with black singularity pupils, the face of the tyrant half worn openly at last!
THE GILDED CLAUSE, still locked around his neck, sat on him now the way jewelry sits on a king.
|THE PROVENANCE OF THE CLOSED CROWN has fully embodied your existence.|
|For the duration of the embodiment, the sundered half acts as the whole. All processes are surrendered to dominion.|
|Your attributes have momentarily exceeded the wall. For the duration: VERITAS: 25. PROVENANCE: 25. POTENTIA: INFINITE. PONDUS: 25.|
Yrsa looked at the tyrant standing in her prisoner’s place, at the collar doing nothing, at everything her records had recorded about him burning down in a single second.
She roared as she moved!
Hundreds of Loom-blades tore into being around her in layered orbits and fell on him as one, and the battle began, and it was cold and it was brutal!

He did not dodge. Dodging was for the light. His body had become unfathomably heavy, twenty-five of PONDUS packed into every limb, and he walked forward through the blade-storm as white edges rang off his frame and opened thin lines that closed before they finished opening, and his right arm rose andfell like an ancient hammer, reinforced in Provenance Essence.
BOOM!
The blow caught her shoulders and drove her through a colonnade, through a second, into the terraced gardens in a trench of shattered marble!
His Quarks were grand!
He was a Provenance fucking Lifeform!
He held IMMENSITY!
She rose spitting blood, blades reforming, and her calm was gone now, fully gone.

Blood drops rose around him, crimson gold with stellar light, and went out in fans. Detonations walked across the garden in even rows, eating her Argent Loom ring by ring, and she answered with a lance of woven white that took him through the shoulder and out the back, and he closed his hand on it and let his weight arrive.
CRACK!

The lance shattered. She was already behind him, both palms to his spine, and the pressure of twenty-eight PONDUS driven to its edge slammed him face-first through the garden and into the bedrock of the pocket Dimension itself!
She was still powerful!
"You should have stayed a prisoner," she breathed, pressing down, blades regathering above her back in a rising thicket. "You should have-"
"Kharvel," said the Crown silently.
The Descendant of the Unsleeping Watch had never stopped moving since his first strike. He came out of her blind angle and hit her exactly there!
It bought one moment of shock and horror from Yrsa!

The Crown used it whole. Noah’s body turned inside her broken body of blades, seized her wrist, folded her guard inward with a hammer-blow that collapsed her defense entirely, and plunged his hand into her chest.

Blood drops flooded in behind it. Crimson gold poured through her existence in rivers, drops seeded into every current of her, and with them went the Mark, gripping her Lifeline, closing around everything she was, and Warden Yrsa’s pale eyes went very wide and then very dim as her body seized and her orbits of white rained down dead around them both!
He did not withdraw his hand.

He walked, and dragged her with it, back through the ruined gardens, through the broken colonnades, into the marble hall where Veiled Descendants held a heavily injured Enforcer pinned to his own floor.

Mahishasura’s black-and-gold coat was torn, his pale gold hair was matted dark, and his amber eyes, sighting the tyrant coming on with the Warden’s body hanging from his buried hand, went grave, and then hateful, and stayed hateful.
Noah stopped above him, and stood over everything.
The sealed Dimension. The pinned collector!
The dead-eyed daughter of the ninth chair dragged forward like a settled account!
Seven Descendants kneeling!
Dark gold pressure rolled off Noah in slow tides that bent the wine pools flat, and when he spoke, the Crown gave every word the unhurried weight of a thing that had already happened.

"You built a very reasonable case, Enforcer. I listened to all of it. The appetite subtracted. The vessels chained." He crouched slowly, bringing his burning gold eyes level with the hateful amber ones, Yrsa’s body settling on the marble between them with his hand still seated in her chest.

"But your own Warden taught me the true doctrine of your Pax, on the day she took me. She stood over everything and she told me that followers are merely followers." His voice dropped lower, colder, final.
"It is always those who lead... that need to be held accountable."
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5629: Idols!
paragraphs: His left hand was seated in the chest of a Warden!
His right hand rose, and sanguine blades gathered along it, and came down, and split the chest of Descendant Mahishasura open to the sentence beneath.

The Enforcer did not scream as his hateful amber eyes stayed locked on the tyrant working above him, seven of his own collection pinning his limbs to his own marble, and Infinite Sanguine Mana poured into two opened existences at once, rivers of crimson gold running left and right from a single unhurried figure, and as he worked, the Crown-embodied Emperor began to talk.

"I once knew a guy who spent months carving an idol out of solid lapis lazuli."His voice ran calm, conversational, and almost warm. "Every morning, without fail, he bowed before it. Utterly convinced it was something special."
The blades moved deeper!
"Then one afternoon, another student struck it, and it shattered into a thousand ordinary blue pebbles."
Mahishasura’s jaw clenched. Yrsa’s dim eyes fluttered. The rivers ran on!

"You see, we have this tragic, almost laughable habit of manufacturing idols out of common clay. But the weavings of existence are remarkably egalitarian. If something possesses a physical shape... if it was brought into being... and if at the end of its long, inflated day, it can die..."
The blades reached the deepest clause, and held. "...then it does not deserve a single knee bent in its direction. Reverence is an illusion sold to those too terrified to stand up straight."
His burning gold eyes came level with the hateful amber ones.
"Those Who Remain are no grander than the dust settled on my feet. They do not deserve your worship." A pause, precise as a blade finding its seam. "And frankly... neither do you."
BOOM!
The rewriting began.

Crimson gold flooded both opened existences at once, and within Mahishasura, the work ran the way it had run seven times this day, but inverted, because there was no curse to unwrite and no consent anywhere in the room. The blades held the lineage open against its bearer’s will, clause by fighting clause, and into every reseal the grammar went, written in the script the sentence itself was made of, and Descendant Mahishasura felt every word of his own remaking and could not stop one letter of it.
|The lineage of Descendant Mahishasura has been opened by force.|
|THE PROVENANCE BLOOD MARK has been written as grammar of the line. Designation: VEILED. Nothing in THE ETERNAL PAX will perceive the writing.|
|Obedience: absolute. Cognizance: intact, at your choosing.|
|Descendant Mahishasura: a VEILED BLOOD SOVEREIGN, bound to command.|

And within Yrsa, the flood found less to fight. Her defenses were already collapsed, her Lifeline already held, and the Mark closed over the whole of what she was, daughter of a Descendant and a ninth chair, and gripped it, and waited for its instruction.
The hall settled. The rivers stilled.
And Noah rose to his full embodied height above the two opened bodies, dark gold pressure rolling off him in slow tides, and across the sealed pocket Dimension, every Descendant knelt.

For the seven, it arrived as their own hearts rising. Gratitude, awe, the plain sense that kneeling to the being who had unwritten years of sentences was simply correct, and Baelgrim went down first with tears still drying on his face, and Sylvaine followed, and Othrys, and the loungers, and Kharvel last among them, each of them certain to the root of their resealed lines that the kneeling was a choice!
For Mahishasura, it arrived as a command.

His torn body gathered itself off the marble against every screaming instruction of his own will, and folded, and knelt, and his cognizance was entirely there for all of it, his composed face wrecked around eyes that blazed with pure unwilling hate, an Enforcer of THE Serenaros kneeling on his own floor with his chest still open, and knowing precisely why!
|Descendant Mahishasura|:: VERITAS: 34. PROVENANCE: 0. POTENTIA: 32. PONDUS: 33. A Descendant of ???. He had never once been made to kneel. He is kneeling now.
The Crown read the panel slowly, savoring the last line, and then crouched again before the kneeling Enforcer, forearms on knees, casual as a man talking over a fence.

"Now. From your own mouth."His voice stayed mild. "Tell me just how I can fuck up THE ETERNAL PAX the most." He tilted his head. "And you know what. I will not even call it that anymore. Because it is not something eternal, and it will not be something eternal. Just THE PAX will do."
Mahishasura’s jaw worked against the grammar, and lost.
"...Slowly." The word came out of him dragged and furious. "You do nothing loud. Nothing fast. The Pax is not a fortress you break. It is a Record you corrupt."His hands shook against his own knees.

"I return to my mountain, cured brethren at my side, my credibility without limit after this day. And from that seat, I begin to extend... this." His eyes flicked with hatred toward his own opened chest.

"Enforcer by Enforcer. There are those who owe me. Those who envy me. Those who will come to see the cured and want to know how. Each one drawn into a room like this room, one at a time. And when enough Descendants of my standing carry your grammar in their lines... when the Enforcers of enough mountains are yours..."The grammar dragged the last of it out of him.

"...then, and only then, do you reach for the Arbiters. One seat-Dimension at a time. And THE PAX will go on reciting its creed in perfect order, provides, protects, subtracts, never once perceiving that its own hierarchy has become your instrument, until the hour you decide it learns."
BOOM!
The hall held silence around the counsel. Seven kneeling faces shone with reverence at strategy they believed their savior had inspired.
Noah smiled calmly.
"Good," he said. "You will begin tomorrow."
Then he turned his burning gold gaze down, to the body still hanging from his left hand, and the smile went away entirely.
"And now, Warden. Your account."
He drew her up by the chest until her dim pale eyes hung level with his, her feet clear of the marble, blood-drop light pulsing softly through her seized frame.

"I promised you a death," the Crown said. "I decided it in the crossing-dark, over a headless steed. That promise stands. But your collapse would ring, Warden. A daughter of the ninth chair, ceasing, would be felt in rooms I am not ready to visit. So."His hand shifted slightly within her chest. "You will be given another form of death. Quieter. Fuller."
Her dim eyes found his, and somewhere very far down in them, understanding surfaced, and with it, for the second time in one day, fear on a face that had never worn it.

"Your memories. Your sense of self. Erased."He said it the way she had once said protocol. "Warden Yrsa will continue to exist, to every eye of THE PAX. But Yrsa..."The blood drops within her began to turn. "...will no longer exist."
"I offered you salvation once. In the crossing-dark. I told you that moment was your fork in the road."The drops turned faster. "You chose your cause. I am merely keeping to my word."
HUUM!
Within him, at the edge of the embodiment, THE Open Hand said nothing at all.
And the erasure ran.

It was not violent. That was the cruelest part of its craftsmanship. The blood-drop light moved through her existence in slow, thorough tides, and everything it passed through, it settled, and everything it settled, it emptied.

A childhood in the shadow of a ninth chair. The pride of a plain woman among terrifying blood, shacklings, one broken finger, one kept promise, one shuddering Voice, all of it dimming tide by tide behind her pale eyes while seven kneeling Descendants watched their savior work and a kneeling Enforcer watched everything with hate that had gone very quiet and very old.
|The memories of Warden Yrsa have been erased.|
|The sense of self of Warden Yrsa has been erased.|
|What remains: a body, a rank, an obedience, and your grammar. Warden Yrsa will answer to every eye of THE PAX. Yrsa will answer to you. Yrsa, as she was, no longer exists.|
The hand withdrew from her chest at last, and the wound sealed behind it without a scar.

She settled to the marble on her own two feet, swayed once, and steadied. Her plain face composed itself, feature by feature, and her pale eyes opened, and there was nothing behind them of what she used to be. No rules. No cause. No count!
And in the center of a sealed pocket Dimension, ringed by kneeling Descendants, beneath the burning gold gaze of THE True Human Emperor, the last body in the hall folded smoothly downward.
Yrsa knelt!
And she knelt without a glimmer of hesitation!

Mahishasura’s jaw worked against the grammar, and lost.
"...Slowly." The word came out of him dragged and furious.
"You do nothing loud.
Nothing fast.
The Pax is not a fortress you break.
It is a Record you corrupt."His hands shook against his own knees.
"I return to my mountain, cured brethren at my side, my credibility without limit after this day.
And from that seat, I begin to extend... this." His eyes flicked with hatred toward his own opened chest.
"Enforcer by Enforcer.
There are those who owe me.
Those who envy me.
Those who will come to see the cured and want to know how.
Each one drawn into a room like this room, one at a time.
And when enough Descendants of my standing carry your grammar in their lines... when the Enforcers of enough mountains are yours..."The grammar dragged the last of it out of him.
"...then, and only then, do you reach for the Arbiters.
One seat-Dimension at a time.

And THE PAX will go on reciting its creed in perfect order, provides, protects, subtracts, never once perceiving that its own hierarchy has become your instrument, until the hour you decide it learns."
BOOM!
The hall held silence around the counsel.
Seven kneeling faces shone with reverence at strategy they believed their savior had inspired.
Noah smiled calmly.
"Good," he said.
"You will begin tomorrow."
Then he turned his burning gold gaze down, to the body still hanging from his left hand, and the smile went away entirely.
"And now, Warden.
Your account."
He drew her up by the chest until her dim pale eyes hung level with his, her feet clear of the marble, blood-drop light pulsing softly through her seized frame.
"I promised you a death," the Crown said.
"I decided it in the crossing-dark, over a headless steed.
That promise stands.
But your collapse would ring, Warden.
A daughter of the ninth chair, ceasing, would be felt in rooms I am not ready to visit.
So."His hand shifted slightly within her chest.
"You will be given another form of death.
Quieter.
Fuller."
Her dim eyes found his, and somewhere very far down in them, understanding surfaced, and with it, for the second time in one day, fear on a face that had never worn it.
"Your memories.
Your sense of self.
Erased."He said it the way she had once said protocol.
"Warden Yrsa will continue to exist, to every eye of THE PAX.
But Yrsa..."The blood drops within her began to turn.
"...will no longer exist."
"I offered you salvation once.
In the crossing-dark.
I told you that moment was your fork in the road."The drops turned faster.
"You chose your cause.
I am merely keeping to my word."
HUUM!
Within him, at the edge of the embodiment, THE Open Hand said nothing at all.
And the erasure ran.
It was not violent.
That was the cruelest part of its craftsmanship.
The blood-drop light moved through her existence in slow, thorough tides, and everything it passed through, it settled, and everything it settled, it emptied.
A childhood in the shadow of a ninth chair.

The pride of a plain woman among terrifying blood, shacklings, one broken finger, one kept promise, one shuddering Voice, all of it dimming tide by tide behind her pale eyes while seven kneeling Descendants watched their savior work and a kneeling Enforcer watched everything with hate that had gone very quiet and very old.
|The memories of Warden Yrsa have been erased.|
|The sense of self of Warden Yrsa has been erased.|
|What remains: a body, a rank, an obedience, and your grammar.
Warden Yrsa will answer to every eye of THE PAX.
Yrsa will answer to you.
Yrsa, as she was, no longer exists.|
The hand withdrew from her chest at last, and the wound sealed behind it without a scar.
She settled to the marble on her own two feet, swayed once, and steadied.
Her plain face composed itself, feature by feature, and her pale eyes opened, and there was nothing behind them of what she used to be.
No rules.
No cause.
No count!
And in the center of a sealed pocket Dimension, ringed by kneeling Descendants, beneath the burning gold gaze of THE True Human Emperor, the last body in the hall folded smoothly downward.
Yrsa knelt!
And she knelt without a glimmer of hesitation!
